articles.title: Silent Lynx Exploits WinRAR Flaw to Deploy Reverse Shell in CIS Government Attacks
articles.text:
The threat actor known as Silent Lynx has been attributed to a fresh set of attacks targeting government organizations across the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).
The activity, observed from June 2025 through August 2026, involves four different infection chains that make use of macro-enabled documents, PS2EXE downloaders, GitHub-hosted PowerShell, and crafted WinRAR archives exploiting CVE-2025-8088.
The attacks lead to the deployment of custom reverse shells like FoalShell, Chvost, Laplas, and PickleShell that facilitate interactive remote access to compromised hosts, according to Cisco Talos and Recorded Future Insikt Group, which are tracking the campaign under the monikers UAT-6275 and TAG-193.
"UAT-6275's targeting is concentrated in Central Asia, and the wider CIS region," security researcher Ashley Shen said. "Across the reviewed campaigns, observed victims and lure themes span nine countries: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Russia, and Belarus."
Silent Lynx was first publicly documented by Seqrite Labs in early 2025, highlighting the threat actor's attacks on embassies, lawyers, government-backed banks, and think tanks across Kyrgyzstan and Turkmenistan.
It's assessed to be a Kazakhstan-nexus threat actor active since at least 2020, sharing overlaps with other clusters codenamed YoroTrooper (aka Comrade Saiga, ShadowSilk, and SturgeonPhisher), ShadowSilk, Cavalry Werewolf, and Tomiris.
It's suspected that both UAT-6275 and YoroTrooper are part of the same broader activity cluster, although no direct indicator or toolset overlap has been observed between the two.
Earlier this year, VMRay disclosed that a threat cluster it tracks as Hydra Saiga compromised at least 34 organizations across 8 countries since December 2024, with reconnaissance efforts extending to over 200 additional targets across the world.
It's worth noting that both Comrade Saiga and Hydra Saiga refer to the same threat actor. The "hydra" prefix in the tracking alias is a reference to the adversary's heavy focus on breaching infrastructure linked specifically to water resources in Central Asia using a mix of custom implants written in Rust, Go, and Python and Living-off-the-Land techniques.
Attack chains mounted by the threat actor involve the use of spear-phishing emails containing diplomatic relations, international trade, energy, and aviation-themed decoy documents. No less than eight campaigns have been identified across the region between January 2025 and May 2026.
The phishing emails are sent from compromised government accounts and make use of official-looking documents to lend the social engineering attack a veneer of credibility. "Identified lures included a diplomatic letter addressed to Armenia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, a Turkmenistan airspace application form, and a business proposal concerning Russia’s Orsk Oil Refinery," Recorded Future said.
What's more, three publicly accessible staging directories linked to the threat actor have been found to host Linux-compatible tooling and a publicly available proof-of-concept exploit for CVE-2025-25257, an SQL injection flaw in Fortinet FortiWeb, suggesting a possible expansion of the threat actor's operational capabilities.
Infection sequences have been found to employ four different pathways -
- June 2025 - Using macro-enabled Word documents to download and run a second-stage binary.
- July 2025 - Using downloaders built with PS2EXE, a tool that packages PowerShell scripts as Windows executables, to fetch reverse-shell payloads and create scheduled tasks for persistence.
- October 2025 - Using a malicious shortcut (LNK) within a RAR archive to launch PowerShell responsible for retrieving and executing a GitHub-hosted script that provides remote shell access. Subsequent iterations also download PickleShell and stage it in the Windows Startup folder so that it's automatically launched every time a user logs in to the system.
- April 2026 - Using a RAR archive that exploits a WinRAR flaw (CVE-2025-8088) to drop PickleShell in the Windows Startup folder.
The April 2026 infection chain marks the first time UAT-6275 has weaponized a security flaw as part of its malware delivery methods.
"UAT-6275's sustained activity and adoption of new delivery techniques suggest the group will continue pursuing access to government organizations across Central Asia and the CIS," Talos said. "Its interest in environmental agencies, economic ministries, and energy infrastructure reflects the intelligence value of regional diplomacy and resource management."

articles.title: Le Grand Orient de France touché par une fuite de données, des noms de membres exposés
articles.text:
737 fichiers attribués au Grand Orient de France ont été mis en ligne récemment. L’obédience a porté plainte et assure que ses systèmes centraux n’ont pas été percés. Des noms de francs-maçons, avec leurs coordonnées, sont maintenant lisibles par n’importe qui dans ces documents.
Créé sous son nom actuel en 1773, le Grand Orient de France est la plus ancienne obédience maçonnique du pays, et beaucoup de ses membres préfèrent garder leur appartenance pour eux. Le pirate à l’origine de la mise en ligne se réclame de deux groupes hacktivistes, et ces groupes ont revendiqué l’opération au nom d’« incidents liés à l’islam », d’après Le Figaro. L’obédience affirme pour sa part qu’aucun intrus n’est entré dans ses serveurs centraux. L’origine exacte des fichiers est donc inconnue, et les francs-maçons cités dans l’archive voient exposée une appartenance protégée de près par le droit européen.
Le Grand Orient conteste toute intrusion dans ses serveurs
Le Grand Orient de France a annoncé hier le dépôt d’une plainte, et une enquête est en cours. D’après ses vérifications techniques, ses systèmes d’information centraux, protégés par une double authentification, « n’ont pas été compromis ». Pour l’obédience, une part importante des fichiers diffusés est faite de communiqués ou de discours sans caractère sensible.
FrenchBreaches a repéré un tableau nominatif daté du 2 septembre 2024 et rattaché à une loge d’Angoulême. Plusieurs dizaines d’entrées sont inscrites sur ces deux pages, avec les adresses e-mail personnelles et les numéros de téléphone des personnes listées.
Le Grand Orient refuse de commenter le contenu des documents tant que l’enquête est en cours, et pour FrenchBreaches, impossible de dire à ce stade comment ils ont été réunis. Il ne suffit d’ailleurs pas d’une revendication sur un forum pour prouver un piratage de serveurs. Le pirate Varun avait ainsi accédé en février 2025 à une centaine d’espaces clients d’EDF avec des identifiants volés ailleurs, sans jamais entrer dans les serveurs de l’entreprise.
Membres du Grand Orient, une appartenance exposée
Pour la CNIL, les convictions religieuses ou philosophiques font partie des données dites sensibles, dont la collecte et l’usage sont en principe interdits. Le Grand Orient de France a toutefois le droit de tenir le fichier de ses adhérents, en tant qu’association philosophique. Avec cette archive proposée au téléchargement sur le forum, n’importe quel internaute peut donc apprendre qu’un collègue ou un voisin fréquente une loge.
Le pirate présente cette publication en avertissement à l’obédience, sur fond de griefs religieux, et menace de lancer des attaques plus violentes. Un escroc peut aussi écrire à un membre au sujet d’une cotisation ou d’une réunion, avec assez de détails internes pour passer pour l’obédience, prévient FrenchBreaches, sans avoir trouvé pour l’instant de preuve d’une telle exploitation. Les membres concernés peuvent obtenir une aide gratuite auprès du dispositif public Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr en cas de message suspect au nom de l’obédience.
Dans son message du 11 octobre, le pirate parle d’une première partie, et le contenu d’éventuels nouveaux envois est inconnu.

articles.title: Tesla presentó el nuevo deportivo Roadster: posee un “sistema de vuelo” y acelera de 0 a 100 km/h en menos de un segundo
articles.text:
Tesla presentó el jueves una versión rediseñada de su auto deportivo eléctrico Roadster, equipada con propulsores y desarrollada junto con SpaceX, y anunció que la producción del vehículo comenzará en 2028. La presentación buscó mostrar un rodado de altas prestaciones en un momento en que la empresa orienta sus recursos hacia la conducción autónoma basada en inteligencia artificial y la robótica.
El nuevo Roadster tendría un papel comercial limitado, pero aspira a convertirse en la vitrina tecnológica de la compañía. Tesla exhibió el vehículo en un centro de pruebas de SpaceX en McGregor, Texas. Durante la demostración, el coche circuló boca abajo por una rampa mediante un sistema de succión, giró en el aire y aterrizó con ayuda de propulsores integrados.
El director ejecutivo de Tesla, Elon Musk, afirmó que el automóvil podrá acelerar de cero a 100 km/h en menos de un segundo y superar los 370 km/h de velocidad máxima. La presentación recuperó un proyecto que Tesla había anticipado en 2017. En aquel momento, la compañía aseguró que las entregas comenzarían en 2020, una meta que finalmente no se cumplió.
Musk y otros ejecutivos no informaron un precio objetivo durante el evento. Hace casi una década, Tesla había mencionado un valor base de USD 200.000 para el automóvil. Después de la presentación, la página de reservas de Tesla mostró una versión “Performance”, para la que exige un depósito de USD 50.000, y también apareció una variante “Thrust”, equipada con “propulsores de aceleración” y con un depósito requerido de USD 250.000.
La oferta incluye además un modelo denominado “Rocket”, disponible “solo por invitación”. “Listo para volar con asiento para una persona. Cuenta con un sistema de succión multimodo combinado con propulsores de gas frío ubicados alrededor del perímetro del vehículo que permiten una aceleración hacia adelante y hacia arriba, así como un movimiento de rotación lateral. Así que sí, puede volar”, indicó Tesla. A su vez, se describe a esta versión como un vehículo monoplaza con un “sistema de vuelo completo”. “Nota: No aprobado para uso en la vía pública”, agrega la página oficial de la empresa.
El modelo retoma el vehículo con el que Tesla comenzó su historia
El Roadster original salió al mercado en 2008 y se vendió hasta 2012. Fue el primer vehículo eléctrico de Tesla y utilizaba el chasis del Lotus Elise. Ese rodado contribuyó a modificar la percepción sobre las posibilidades de los coches eléctricos, al asociarlos con rendimiento y diseño deportivo en lugar de vehículos limitados para trayectos cortos.
Desde entonces, Tesla consolidó su negocio con los SUV Model Y y Model X, además de los sedanes Model S y Model 3. El Roadster de segunda generación llega cuando la empresa ya no presenta a los automóviles convencionales como el eje exclusivo de su futuro.
Este año, Tesla dejó de vender los modelos S y X para liberar capacidad de producción destinada a sus robots humanoides Optimus.
La compañía también lanzó Cybercab, un robotaxi de dos plazas sin volante, pedales ni espejos. Con ese cambio de enfoque, el nuevo Roadster queda planteado como una excepción: un coche diseñado para conducir, exhibir prestaciones y sostener el prestigio tecnológico de Tesla.
El Roadster no parece destinado a convertirse en un producto de gran volumen para Tesla. Musk lo definió en 2023 como una “situación sin importancia” y sostuvo que no tendría un impacto significativo en las finanzas de la empresa.
Esa mirada contrasta con el lugar que el vehículo puede ocupar dentro de la marca. El analista de Morningstar Seth Goldstein consideró que Tesla necesita un automóvil que represente sus capacidades técnicas en el segmento de lujo.
“Actualmente, Tesla no cuenta con un modelo insignia, es decir, un vehículo de lujo de alto rendimiento diseñado para mostrar lo mejor de la ingeniería y la tecnología del fabricante. El Roadster será el nuevo modelo insignia de Tesla”, afirmó Goldstein en una nota a Reuters el mes pasado.
El analista proyectó que Tesla podría vender alrededor de 2.000 Roadsters por año. Esa cifra representaría una porción reducida frente a los 1,6 millones de vehículos que la compañía comercializó el año pasado. La importancia del modelo, entonces, no estaría en su volumen de ventas. Su función sería reforzar la percepción de Tesla como fabricante capaz de llevar prestaciones poco habituales a un vehículo eléctrico.
(Con información de Reuters)

articles.title: Volodymyr Zelenskyy claims China will transfer a Starlink-alternative to Moscow that could allow Russia to 'dominate the skies over Ukraine'
articles.text:
Volodymyr Zelenskyy claims China will transfer a Starlink-alternative to Moscow that could allow Russia to 'dominate the skies over Ukraine'
Zelenskyy says China is handing Russia the tech for its own Starlink
- Zelenskyy says China is passing Russia technology for a Starlink alternative that could give Moscow dominance in Ukraine's skies
- The system is Bureau 1440's Rassvet, which has launched 32 satellites against a 2026 plan of 156 and has lost at least one
- Kyiv has not publicly named any Chinese firms or shown evidence, and Beijing has previously rejected similar accusations even as Ukraine aims to push for US permission to use Starlink over Russia to hunt missile launchers
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says China is giving Russia the technology to build its own version of Starlink and warns it could give Moscow a decisive edge in the skies over Ukraine.
Zelenskyy made the remarks to reporters in Pryluky, where a Russian cruise missile struck an apartment building on October 7 2026, killing 22 people, including five children.
He said he has been telling partners in the US and Europe that China is working on alternatives to Starlink. "They're getting closer. They're passing this on to Russia. Russia could end up dominating," he said, according to LIGA.net's translation.
A warning months in the making even if the impact so far is limited
This isn't a new narrative from Kyiv; In August, Zelenskyy said Russia was developing its own answer to Starlink with Chinese help and expected it to be ready by December 2026.
On September 30, Ukraine's acting ambassador in Washington, Denys Sienik, urged the US to sanction entities behind Russia's Rassvet satellite network, warning that a launch by year's end would let Russia "hit Ukrainian targets in real time on our territory," with Reuters describing those entities as Russian.
Three days later, Zelenskyy told the Financial Times he had asked Donald Trump several times, most recently on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, to sanction the Russian and Chinese firms involved, saying Beijing "works on the possibility of helping Russia with a similar Starlink." On October 4, he went further, telling journalists that "the Chinese will share with Russia" relevant technology around the turn of the year.
The network at the center of all this is Rassvet ("Dawn"), built by Bureau 1440, a subsidiary of Russia's IKS Holding. Its first 16 production satellites launched in March, around three months late, and a second batch of 16 followed in July, for a total of 32 satellites so far.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Russia's federal rollout plan called for 156 satellites in 2026 and 292 by 2027, which means that with less than three months of the year left, Russia has launched roughly a fifth of this year's target.
The satellites that do exist have had a rough ride. Rassvet-3 No. 4 never raised its orbit and reentered the atmosphere on June 6; two satellites from the July batch showed no orbit-raising maneuvers, and none had reached the roughly 800 km target altitude by late August. Ukraine's military intelligence chief, Oleh Ivashchenko, says there are still too few satellites and their effectiveness is low, and his deputy, Vadym Skibitskyi, said Russia uses Rassvet "in a fragmented manner, only once the satellites pass over Ukrainian territory."
No Chinese firms named yet
Zelenskyy has not named a particular Chinese firm yet; if Beijing is helping, the clearest signs point to internal components, not a complete network. Bureau 1440 says it develops its satellites' key modules in-house, but experts interviewed by Ukrainian outlet Militarnyi said much of the core hardware is probably built from off-the-shelf Chinese parts. Other experts point to American and European parts reaching Russia through sanctions-evasion networks, as Euromaidan Press noted.
Russia's wider space industry does lean on China, though: leaked plans to expand Angara rocket production list only 57 Chinese machines out of 541, yet those make up 28.2% of the project's technological core.
One could argue that this is inevitable given both the US's technological dominance in the field and China's stranglehold on the market as a secondary seller to both price-conscious and sanctioned buyers, even as Russia qualifies on both grounds.
The real reason for Zelenskyy pushing is somewhat transparent: Kyiv wants Starlink over Russia to help target infrastructure and military targets alike as the war has spilled onto the former, even as the latter has considerably hardened its defenses of late.
Zelenskyy wants Ukrainian drones to be able to use Starlink to hunt ballistic missile launchers and drone launch sites up to 200 km inside Russia, and says Trump backs the idea but has left the decision to Elon Musk. The pressure here is also tied to air defense. By Zelenskyy's count, Ukraine received 675 Patriot missiles in 2023, 364 in 2025, and 264 so far in 2026.
The slowdown is seen as a mix of Trump's deteriorating relations with the Ukrainian premier, coupled with a shortage of interceptors spurred by an ongoing on-again, off-again conflict between the US and Iran. It also means that Ukraine is hedging its bets rather than simply depending on US help.
Ukrainian firm Stetman plans a 360-satellite constellation built by Denmark's GomSpace and launched by SpaceX from 2027, though only a test satellite launch had been agreed when that plan was reported, and Zelenskyy said in Pryluky that European projects aren't yet close to what Ukraine needs.
None of this makes the warning empty, because Rassvet is real and its coverage is growing. But the strongest version of the claim, that Chinese technology will hand Moscow control of Ukraine's skies within months, runs north of the established public record.
For now, China's role is asserted without named companies, and the constellation sits at roughly a fifth of its 2026 target. Whether Washington moves on sanctions, or on Starlink access over Russia, before that launch schedule catches up may matter more than the rhetoric that has been ongoing for a long time.
This is even as Ukraine vies for more support at a time when Donald Trump has just clinched an expanding deal with Russia for diesel in what many feel is a somewhat desperate bid to save Republican polling numbers as midterms loom next month.

articles.title: SK Hynix conditionne sa nouvelle usine aux États-Unis à plus d’exportations d’équipements de puces vers la Chine
articles.text:
Donald Trump fait tout pour attirer les géants des semi-conducteurs sur le territoire américain. Mais avec SK Hynix, il va devoir faire des efforts sur sa guerre avec la Chine.
L'administration actuelle à Washington veut que les géants des semi-conducteurs conduisent beaucoup plus aux États-Unis. Sont concernés évidemment TSMC, mais aussi les Sud-Coréens Samsung et SK Hynix. Le premier continue ainsi d'injecter des milliards de dollars sur le territoire américain, quand le second pose ses conditions pour suivre une trajectoire similaire !
Si Donald Trump veut plus de production SK Hynix aux USA, il faudra l'autoriser à travailler en Chine
SK Hynix va devoir produire plus aux États-Unis ? Eh bien, ça sera donnant-donnant selon une nouvelle information de Reuters. En effet, le géant sud-coréen des composants mémoires veut que Washington fasse un effort.
Plus exactement, le groupe veut que Washington l'autorise à exporter plus d'équipements de production de puces américains en Chine. Car SK Hynix veut augmenter sa production globale, et ça passera par son usine située à Dalian (dans le Nord de la Chine, à proximité de la péninsulte coréenne).
L'administration Trump avait retiré l'an dernier les autorisations de Samsung et SK Hynix relatives à la production en Chine
La filiale américaine SK Hynix, Solidigm, compte de l'espace inoccupé sur ce site de Dalian, spécialisé dans la mémoire NAND - une espace qu'elle veut mettre à profit dorénavant, vu l'explosion de la demande. Mais le site de Dalian utilise des équipements de productions américains venant notamment de Lam Research, Applied Materials et KLA. D'où la nécessité d'obtenir une autorisation de Washington.
SK Hynix (tout comme Samsung) bénéficiait jusqu'à l'année dernière d'autorisations lui permettant d'importer ces équipements américains sur ces sites de production chinois. Des autorisations révoquées en 2025 par le département du Commerce, qui avait qualifié ces autorisations de « faille juridique de l'ère Biden ». Reste à voir si l'exécutif américain acceptera cette demande, alors que le découplage USA/Chine devient toujours plus important.

articles.title: Help TDS Linked to Hotejka as 20,000+ Cloudflare Pages Domains Host Tech Support Scams
articles.text:
A long-running Traffic Distribution System (TDS) known as Help TDS to a Russian-language affiliate program called Hotejka, which appears to be a rebrand of a traffic monetization operation dubbed ROI777.
Help TDS is assessed to be active since at least 2017, offering PHP code templates to partners and affiliates that are installed into compromised websites with an aim to direct unsuspecting users to tech support scams. These scams make use of full-screen browser manipulation and exit prevention techniques to serve bogus Microsoft Windows security alert screens instructing victims to contact a Windows Support number to address the problem.
"Help TDS delivers tech support scams (TSSs) that direct users to call centers, where social engineering is used to convince them to install remote desktop tools," Infoblox said in a report shared with The Hacker News. "It's not simple credit card fraud: it's remote access, living-off-the-land malware operations. Once in, the threat actor can exploit the victim time and again."
Help TDS's evolution was documented by GoDaddy in August 2025, highlighting the threat actor's use of a malicious WordPress plugin named "woocommerce_inputs" on thousands of websites to steal WordPress user credentials and facilitate the malicious redirections by fetching the URLs from its command-and-control (C2) servers. The plugin, or alternatively a custom HTML block, is injected into the sites by Hotejka's affiliates.
Historical tracking of malicious redirect chains has also uncovered that Help TDS has routinely handed off traffic directly to VexTrio Viper, a cybercrime operator that runs an affiliate program to enable scams, riskware, spyware, adware, and pornographic content.
The latest findings connect the TDS to Hotejka, which, in turn, is suspected to be a successor to ROI777, an entity that was exposed by Guardicore Labs (now part of Akamai) in June 2018 in connection with a traffic manipulation and cryptocurrency mining campaign codenamed Operation Prowli.
The activity involved the compromise of vulnerable servers to deploy a malware named r2r2 and then leverage them to mine cryptocurrency. In tandem, WordPress sites and servers running other content management systems (CMS) were exploited for traffic monetization fraud.
"Traffic monetizers, such as ROI777, buy traffic from 'website operators' such as the Prowli attackers and redirect it to domains on demand," Guardicore Labs noted at the time. "Website 'operators' earn money per traffic sent through roi777. The destination domains frequently host different scams, such as fake services, malicious browser extensions and more."
The rebrand is believed to be driven by the leak of data obtained from ROI777's servers in March 2018, around when it was operating Disposable TDS, a precursor to Help TDS. The published details included Telegram identities of its users and specifics about multiple campaigns.
The connection between Hotejka and ROI77 doesn't end there, for GoDaddy also found that "roi777[.]com" was one of the historical C2 domains used between 2018 and 2020 to fetch the redirect domains.
"[Hotejka's] affiliates range from spam operators to website compromisers," Infoblox said. "Potential victims are redirected into the TDS from these affiliates via special URLs provided by Hotejka. The TDS then evaluates the user via browser fingerprinting and location to determine the course of action."
A TDS functions akin to a relay, intercepting internet traffic from compromised websites, malicious ads, social media posts, or SEO spam, analyzing the visitor, filter traffic based on predefined criteria (e.g., geographic location, device metadata, IP reputation, and headless browsers), and dynamically route them to scams, browser lockers, or malware drops.
"Help TDS and its precursors are the routing decision infrastructure for a small affiliate program," Infoblox explained. "Other threat actors, for example ones who have compromised websites, send potential victim traffic to the TDS through specially crafted URLs."
The TDS is believed to be implemented on Keitaro, an advertising performance tracking platform that's known to be abused by various threat actors. Some of the initial Help TDS lures prompt users of an impending Windows update, followed by a warning that the machine has been disabled by Microsoft, tells them not to restart the computer, and that a "computer lock" has been put in place to block illegal activity.
The scareware prompt is designed to persuade the victim to contact the Microsoft Technical Support team. Should the victim make the phone call, the threat actor on the other end instructs them to download and install a free remote desktop tool like Ultraviewer to gain complete control of the infected machine.
The fingerprinting step determines whether to route the user to either the tech support scam or to another affiliate marketing platform, which then evaluates the device again and resells the traffic. These pathways lead to scam landing pages with fake CAPTCHA checks to enroll the victim's browser to push-notification spam.
"Historical DNS records, loyal use of other affiliate advertising platforms over the years, and consistent command-and-control (C2) mechanisms give us a high degree of confidence that ROI777 and Hotejka are one and the same," Infoblox said.
Messages posted by Hotejka on their Telegram channel (@hotejka_hot) demonstrate their criminal intent by advertising forced browser extension installations and tech support landing pages that are "very difficult to exit." In one post dated July 17, 2026, the operator claimed a "small call center in Germany will handle 50-100 calls per day."
Since April 2026, the scams are run on free Cloudflare Pages sites (*.pages[.]dev), with the threat actor creating roughly 300 disposable pages per day. Over 20,000 such domains have been detected since then. In recent years, Hotejka has also been observed using different aliases on forums like CrackingX, seeking traffic from email spam and access to WordPress admin panels for prices starting at $100.
In all, about 20 different affiliates, including Balada Injector, Detour Dog, and DollyWay, send traffic to Help TDS. These operations are known to heavily target WordPress sites to redirect victims to scams and malware.
"Hotejka/ROI777 has been loyal to the two affiliate platforms since 2017, and we believe that loyalty has paid handsomely," Infoblox said. "Using DNS volumes observed over the past 8 years, our ability to use affiliate IDs to track traffic over time, and commonly cited payout figures for affiliate advertising in general, we suspect that the two European programs have paid them at least a few million dollars (USD)."

articles.title: Call of Duty Modern Warfare 4 Will be an "Epic Conclusion" with a New Sub-Franchise To Follow
articles.text:
Thursday, October 15th 2026
Call of Duty Modern Warfare 4 Will be an "Epic Conclusion" with a New Sub-Franchise To Follow
At best, Call of Duty Black Ops 7 has had a mixed reception since it launched in November 2025, and at worst, it has left a "Mostly Negative" impression on its audience, per the Steam review rating. However, it seems as though Activision is taking lessons from the launch of Black Ops 7 and rethinking how it approaches the Call of Duty franchise altogether. According to Activision chief marketing officer, Tyler Bahl, in an interview with The Game Business, Activision will be moving away from the current structure of long-standing sub-franchises with many consecutive games in a series, and it will be the "epic conclusion for this recent series of Modern Warfare," although he hints that some characters may reappear later or be reinvented for other games. 
Bahl comments that Activision isn't happy with every aspect of Black Ops 7, and it is taking community feedback seriously, which is stated to be one of the reasons it previously announced that Modern Warfare 4 would be going back to Call of Duty's more realistic roots, with "no BS," referring to outlandish skins, collaborations, and other content. He adds that Modern Warfare 4 is "getting back to a grounded, military shooter; really making it cinematic, making it authentic, and bringing that edge back that Call of Duty is known for."The full interview is available below.

articles.title: Cómo saber si alguien revisa tu WhatsApp sin permiso: la función que ayuda a proteger tu cuenta
articles.text:
WhatsApp cuenta con una función que permite revisar en qué computadoras, tabletas y otros dispositivos está abierta una cuenta, una herramienta útil para detectar accesos que el usuario no reconoce. Se trata de Dispositivos vinculados, una opción que muestra las sesiones asociadas a la aplicación y permite cerrar aquellas que no hayan sido autorizadas.
La herramienta cobra importancia porque una cuenta puede utilizarse desde otro equipo mediante la vinculación de dispositivos. Si una persona consigue acceso físico al celular y logra vincular una computadora o un segundo dispositivo, podría consultar las conversaciones desde ese equipo mientras la sesión permanezca activa.
Sin embargo, encontrar un dispositivo desconocido no demuestra por sí solo que alguien haya leído los mensajes. Por eso, WhatsApp permite revisar las sesiones abiertas y desconectar aquellas que generen sospechas, además de ofrecer otras medidas para reforzar la seguridad de la cuenta.
Cómo revisar si alguien tiene acceso a tu WhatsApp
La función Dispositivos vinculados permite consultar los equipos asociados a una cuenta y comprobar cuándo estuvieron activos por última vez. Para revisar esta información, basta con seguir unos pasos desde el celular.
En Android, el procedimiento es el siguiente:
- Abre WhatsApp en el teléfono.
- Pulsa el menú de tres puntos situado en la parte superior derecha.
- Selecciona Dispositivos vinculados.
- Revisa la lista de equipos y la última actividad registrada.
En iPhone, el acceso se encuentra en la pestaña Configuración, ubicada en la parte inferior de la aplicación. Desde allí, selecciona Dispositivos vinculados para consultar las sesiones activas.
Si aparece una computadora, un navegador u otro equipo que no reconoces, puedes seleccionarlo y cerrar la sesión desde esa misma pantalla. Si tienes dudas sobre varias sesiones, revisa cada una antes de desconectarla.
Esta función no permite identificar directamente a la persona que utilizó el dispositivo ni confirmar qué conversaciones consultó. Su utilidad consiste en mostrar las sesiones vinculadas para que el titular pueda detectar accesos desconocidos y tomar medidas.
Qué hacer si encuentras un dispositivo desconocido
Si identificas una sesión que no autorizaste, lo recomendable es cerrarla inmediatamente. Después, revisa las medidas de seguridad de tu cuenta y evita dejar el teléfono desbloqueado al alcance de otras personas.
También puedes activar la verificación en dos pasos, una función que añade un PIN de seis dígitos al proceso de registro del número telefónico en WhatsApp. Para configurarla, ingresa en Ajustes o Configuración, selecciona Cuenta y después Verificación en dos pasos. Sigue las indicaciones para crear el código y, si la aplicación lo permite, añade una dirección de correo electrónico para facilitar la recuperación.
Este mecanismo ofrece una capa adicional de protección, aunque no sustituye el bloqueo del celular ni impide que alguien con acceso autorizado al teléfono pueda leer los mensajes directamente.
Otra recomendación es mantener WhatsApp actualizado y evitar aplicaciones no oficiales que prometan funciones adicionales. Descargar programas de fuentes desconocidas puede exponer los datos personales o facilitar el acceso no autorizado al dispositivo.
Señales que pueden despertar sospechas en WhatsApp
Existen comportamientos que pueden llamar la atención, como mensajes que aparecen como leídos sin que el usuario los haya abierto, conversaciones enviadas que no recuerda haber escrito o cambios en la cuenta que no realizó.
No obstante, estas señales no prueban necesariamente que alguien esté espiando los chats. Un mensaje puede marcarse como leído por una notificación abierta en otro dispositivo, mientras que los problemas de rendimiento, el sobrecalentamiento o el consumo elevado de batería pueden deberse a distintas causas.
Por eso, antes de concluir que existe una intrusión, conviene revisar los dispositivos vinculados, comprobar la actividad de la cuenta y analizar si hay otros indicios de acceso no autorizado.
Cómo proteger las conversaciones y la cuenta
Además de cerrar sesiones desconocidas y activar la verificación en dos pasos, es importante utilizar un bloqueo de pantalla seguro y no compartir el PIN de registro ni los códigos de verificación recibidos por SMS.
WhatsApp también ofrece opciones de privacidad, como el bloqueo de chats, que permite proteger determinadas conversaciones mediante autenticación adicional. Estas herramientas ayudan a reducir el riesgo de que otra persona acceda a información privada si consigue utilizar el teléfono.
Revisar periódicamente los dispositivos vinculados es una medida sencilla para detectar sesiones que no se reconocen. Aunque no garantiza que nadie haya accedido a una cuenta, permite identificar conexiones sospechosas y actuar antes de que continúen activas.

articles.title: Meta et Apple s’allient pour faire tourner une IA de 816 milliards de paramètres sur Mac
articles.text:
Avec deux Mac Studio M5 Ultra reliés entre eux, un développeur pourra bientôt faire tourner chez lui le modèle ouvert le plus performant conçu à ce jour aux États-Unis, à en croire Meta. Le groupe de Mark Zuckerberg a mis au point Muse Spark Open avec Apple, son adversaire de longue date sur la vie privée.
Mark Zuckerberg a remercié John Ternus, à la tête d’Apple depuis le 1er septembre, dans un message que vous pouvez lire ci-dessous, dans lequel il assure que le modèle « fonctionne à merveille sur les nouveaux Mac Studio ». Les deux entreprises travaillent ensemble depuis plusieurs mois, et Daniel Gross, ancien cadre d’Apple passé chez Meta, a joué les entremetteurs, d’après Alexandr Wang, patron de l’IA chez Meta, interrogé par Axios. « Nous sommes ravis de voir papa et maman se réconcilier », a-t-il plaisanté. Pour charger le modèle, il faudra tout de même un téraoctet de mémoire unifiée et Apple ne commercialisera qu’à la fin octobre la déclinaison 512 Go du Mac Studio M5 Ultra, sans laquelle il est impossible de réunir ce téraoctet avec deux machines. Encore faut-il comprendre comment un modèle de cette taille tient sur deux ordinateurs de bureau, et ce que coûte une telle installation.
Un téraoctet pour 816 milliards de paramètres
Meta a conçu Muse Spark Open pour la programmation et les tâches d’agent de longue haleine. Nativement multimodal, avec une fenêtre de contexte d’un million de jetons, le modèle compte 816 milliards de paramètres, mais seuls 42 milliards d’entre eux sont sollicités à chaque jeton généré. Grâce à ce fonctionnement, il suffit de deux Mac Studio pour faire tourner l’ensemble, d’après le billet de lancement de Meta. Le modèle doit être chargé en entier en mémoire, et Apple laisse le GPU intégré à la puce M5 Ultra utiliser jusqu’à 512 Go de mémoire unifiée par machine. Avec une bande passante mémoire de 1,2 To/s, la petite fraction de paramètres nécessaire à chaque jeton est lue assez vite par la puce. « Résultat, deux Mac Studio se comportent comme un seul supercalculateur doté d’un téraoctet de mémoire unifiée », résume le laboratoire.
Le premier modèle de la famille Muse, Muse Spark, était réservé à sa sortie en avril aux applications de Meta et à une API en accès restreint, sans possibilité de télécharger ses poids, ces milliards de valeurs numériques fixées pendant l’entraînement. Meta avait alors promis d’ouvrir de futures versions. Ses équipes ont testé cette déclinaison ouverte entièrement en local, avec leur outil de programmation Muse Code. Elles lui ont fait corriger des bugs et ajouter des fonctions au client Mastodon open source Ice Cubes, sur iOS, jusqu’à compiler une version complète. Elles l’ont aussi chargé de piloter le logiciel de montage DaVinci Resolve de bout en bout, avec un examen image par image des vidéos pour en isoler les meilleurs moments et les recadrer à la verticale.
Près de 50 000 euros pour une installation à domicile
Apple n’a pas dévoilé le prix du Mac Studio 512 Go. Il est toutefois possible de faire tourner Muse Spark Open sur quatre Mac Studio M5 Ultra de 256 Go, et chacun coûte 12 429 euros en France avec 1 To de stockage. L’addition dépasse 49 700 euros, contre environ 38 000 dollars outre-Atlantique d’après les calculs d’Engadget. Un développeur amateur aura du mal à suivre. Les entreprises qui dépensent sans compter en jetons auprès des fournisseurs d’IA peuvent en revanche trouver leur compte dans l’achat de quelques machines, estime le site, à condition que le modèle tienne ses promesses. Meta fournit les seuls chiffres de performance disponibles, et dans ses tests, Muse Spark Open est devant les modèles chinois GLM 5.3 et Kimi K3 sur les tâches d’agent et le raisonnement visuel. Pour le groupe, les États-Unis ne doivent pas laisser les laboratoires chinois dominer l’IA ouverte.
En local, Meta ne reçoit aucune des requêtes envoyées au modèle. « Meta n’a aucun contrôle ni aucune visibilité sur tout cela », a insisté Alexandr Wang. Avec ce fonctionnement, Apple et Meta évitent aussi le sujet de la vie privée, sur lequel Tim Cook et Mark Zuckerberg ont longtemps croisé le fer. Sans budget matériel, les développeurs peuvent télécharger les poids du modèle ou passer par des plateformes d’API, dont Groq et OpenRouter. Meta diffuse ces poids sous une licence maison aux conditions commerciales limitées, et de nombreux développeurs pourront utiliser le modèle gratuitement.
Apple et Meta seront toujours concurrents sur d’autres terrains, a reconnu Alexandr Wang. « Là où il est logique de collaborer et de nouer des partenariats, nous voulons pouvoir le faire », a-t-il ajouté.

articles.title: The new Lego 2026 Advent calendars are a festive delight, with everything from Spider-Man on skis, to Grogu in a Holiday sweater, or a traditional Santa's workshop scene
articles.text:
Lego's 2026 Advent calendars are such a festive delight that they're starting to sell out already — now's a smart time to grab one of 6 new sets
These buildable countdown calendars are packed with charming details
Lego's 2026 Advent Calendars are here, and there are six new sets to explore. The Lego City calendar is the traditional option, centered around Santa's workshop, with elves, toys, Mr and Mrs Claus, and snowman figurines. The box transforms into a scene onto which the completed models can sit — a perfect addition to your Holiday decorations.
Marvel and Star Wars fans are catered for, too, with calendars that include fan-favorite characters with a festive twist. There's Doctor Doom angrily enjoying his candy cane, Spider-Man on skis, and Mandalorian, Moff Gideon and Grogu all sporting Holiday sweaters.
Finally, there are a couple more child-focused options; a festive-themed Lego Friends calendar, and a Disney calendar that turns into a board game. The latter includes princesses and their sidekicks kitted out in their holiday best (Cinderella's Gus has antlers), plus buildable scenes like a gingerbread castle and train set.
If you head to Amazon there are also a number of previous years' calendars still available to purchase — including some classics like the Harry Potter sets. Because they're just numbered 1-25 they'll work just as well this year as the year they launched in.
Lego's Advent calendars have proven themselves reliably popular year-in, year-out, and some of the 2026 sets are already showing as sold out in some places. So although it might feel a bit premature to be planning for the holidays in mid-October, now is actually quite a smart time to buy. articles.title: NGINX Fixes 5 Flaws, Including Possible RCE and a TLS Bug That May Skip Client-Cert Checks
articles.text:
NGINX released versions 1.30.6 and 1.31.7 on October 14 to fix five vulnerabilities, one of them present in every release since May 2005.
There are three memory bugs that F5, the company behind NGINX, says could crash a worker process or possibly let an attacker run code, and each requires a specific configuration to exploit.
A fourth lets an attacker forge a TLS session that could get past client-certificate checks, though F5 calls the forgery non-deterministic and beyond the attacker's control. The fifth lets an HTTP/3 client slip extra bytes into a request that NGINX passes on to a backend.
None of the five was in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog as of October 15, and neither NGINX nor F5 reports attacks. NGINX rates all five medium. F5 scores the three memory bugs 9.2, Critical, on CVSS v4.0, the TLS flaw 8.3, and the HTTP/3 flaw 6.9.
Which Configurations Are Exposed
Every one of the five needs a directive you added: an alias with a rewrite, a regex map, AIO with SSI, a shared TLS session cache, or HTTP/3. NGINX's own documentation recommends the shared session cache and request buffering; the other condition for the HTTP/3 flaw is on by default.
The TLS flaw sits in the automatic rotation of session ticket keys. Session tickets let a client resume a TLS session without a full handshake, and since version 1.23.2, from October 2022, a shared session cache makes NGINX generate and rotate the ticket keys itself unless you load keys from a file.
Each worker process keeps a copy of three key slots. Rotation copied only two, so the third slot held whatever was in memory before, and a ticket naming that slot could be verified and decrypted with that uninitialized key material, "allowing a forged session," the fix commit says.
F5 says the forgery works "in a non-deterministic manner that is beyond the attacker's control," and that an attacker could use it to bypass verification of client certificates. The exposed setting, ssl_session_cache shared:SSL:10m, is the one NGINX's documentation uses in its example configuration. NGINX fixed a session-reuse flaw with the same consequence, CVE-2025-23419, in February 2025.
The conditions and workarounds below are NGINX's and F5's. The version ranges are from NGINX's advisories page.
| Flaw | What it allows | Configuration that exposes you | Affected versions | If you cannot upgrade (F5) | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CVE-2026-15176 | Heap overflow in a worker process: crash, possibly code execution | A location with alias, a rewrite that changes the URI, and anything that reads $request_filename (return, set, if, add_header or the access-log format) | 0.1.29 to 1.31.6 | Do not use alias in that location. Do not use $request_filename. | 
| CVE-2026-93479 | Heap overflow in a worker process: crash, possibly code execution | A regex map whose captures are referenced by root or log_format before the map's output variable | 1.30.0 to 1.30.5 and 1.31.2 to 1.31.6 | Use named captures, and use them only inside the block with the regex match. | 
| CVE-2026-97205 | Use-after-free in a worker process: crash, memory corruption, possibly code execution | aio enabled and an SSI page with include virtual commands, in some configurations | 0.8.11 to 1.31.6 | Turn aio off, or do not serve SSI pages. | 
| CVE-2026-95101 | Extra bytes injected into a proxied request, or a body past client_max_body_size | HTTP/3 with proxy_request_buffering on , the default | 1.25.0 to 1.31.6 | Set proxy_request_buffering off. | 
| CVE-2026-97629 | A forged TLS session that could bypass client-certificate verification (non-deterministic and beyond the attacker's control, F5 says) | ssl_session_cache shared:... without ssl_session_ticket_key , which turns on automatic key rotation | 1.23.2 to 1.31.6 | Remove the shared cache directive, or load keys from a file with ssl_session_ticket_key. Servers with ssl_session_tickets off are not affected. | 
One Flaw Traces to July's Fix
The map flaw, CVE-2026-93479, is in the string-handling code that NGINX patched on July 15 for CVE-2026-42533, a heap overflow F5 scored 9.2 that is reached through a regex map's captures.
The new overflow became possible after a change in that July release, according to the fix commit. A July patch added protection against overrunning a buffer, but data could still spill into a reserved area, and a second July patch then sized the final string from that spilled length, so the string could outgrow its buffer.
The commit puts limits on it. The overflow is at most the size of the reserved area on the document-root path, and a single null byte on the access-log path.
F5's advisory and NGINX's advisories page list 1.30.0 and 1.31.2 as the earliest affected versions, which come before the July change. A server patched in July is inside the affected range either way.
F5's July workaround had already been questioned. Researcher Stan Shaw told The Hacker News in July that switching to named captures left a narrower path open, and that upgrading was "the only complete fix."
The fix commits for the alias, AIO and HTTP/3 flaws describe the other three bugs. The alias flaw opens in the moment after a rewrite changes a request's URI and before NGINX picks the next location. If anything reads $request_filename in that window, and the location's prefix is longer than the rewritten URI, mapping the URI to a file path overflows a buffer.
The AIO flaw is a counter. Each pending asynchronous operation on a request adds one to an 8-bit field with no check, so 256 pending operations wrap it to zero and the request can be freed while those operations still point at its memory. NGINX names SSI pages with include virtual commands, which can run their included requests in parallel, as the trigger.
The HTTP/3 flaw came from one parser field doing two jobs: holding the remaining length of an unknown frame being skipped, and the number of DATA bytes to pass on as request body. When an unknown frame was split across two reads, the leftover count was treated as body and sent to the backend, outside the client_max_body_size check.
What to Do
Upgrade to 1.30.6 on the stable branch or 1.31.7 on mainline. The stable release contains only fixes. NGINX publishes fixes for those two branches only, so older branches such as 1.28 stay inside the affected ranges, and a distribution package is fixed only if your distribution has backported the patches.
NGINX Plus customers, and users of F5's Ingress Controller, Gateway Fabric, Instance Manager and WAF products, should check F5's advisories, which list affected builds and, for several products, no fixed build as of October 15.
If you cannot upgrade yet, the table above has F5's workaround for each flaw. To see which paths your server has enabled, print the running configuration with nginx -T and search it for alias beside a rewrite, a regex map used by root or log_format, aio together with ssi, listen lines with quic, and ssl_session_cache shared without ssl_session_ticket_key.
The rewrite-module overflow NGINX patched in May, CVE-2026-42945, was being exploited within days of disclosure, VulnCheck found. This is NGINX's eighth security release of 2026.
F5 credits Matt Suiche of Tolmo and Mateusz Gierblinski with the map flaw, Hansol Lee of GOTROOT with the HTTP/3 flaw, PhiNode Labs with the TLS flaw, and a researcher it names as Cyberlanc3r with the AIO flaw.
F5 found the alias flaw itself. NGINX also released njs 1.0.2 the same day, fixing two medium-severity XML-handling flaws in its JavaScript module, CVE-2026-101025 and CVE-2026-101019.

articles.title: Cómo evitar moho y malos olores en la lavadora con un método de mantenimiento, según fabricantes
articles.text:
El mantenimiento periódico de la lavadora se convirtió en una recomendación constante de fabricantes como LG, Haceb, Samsung y Whirlpool, que advierten sobre la acumulación de suciedad, residuos de detergente y moho dentro del electrodoméstico.
Aunque la lavadora cumple la función de limpiar la ropa, su interior también requiere atención regular para evitar olores desagradables y fallas en su funcionamiento.
La importancia de este cuidado radica en que, con el uso diario, el tambor, los filtros y los compartimentos acumulan humedad y restos de jabón que favorecen la proliferación de bacterias y hongos. Sin una limpieza adecuada, estos residuos pueden afectar tanto el rendimiento del equipo como la frescura de las prendas lavadas.
Con qué frecuencia conviene limpiar el equipo
Según las recomendaciones de los fabricantes, la limpieza de la lavadora debería realizarse cada mes para evitar que la suciedad se acumule de forma excesiva. Algunos modelos incluyen ciclos específicos para esta tarea, conocidos como Tub Clean, diseñados para eliminar residuos de detergente sin intervención manual.
Cuando el electrodoméstico no cuenta con esta función, los fabricantes sugieren revisar de manera mensual el tambor, el filtro de la bomba de drenaje, el dispensador de detergente, los filtros de entrada y las juntas de la puerta. Esta rutina reduce el riesgo de obstrucciones y contribuye a extender la vida útil del equipo.
Pasos recomendados para la limpieza interna
Los fabricantes coinciden en un procedimiento de cinco pasos aplicable tanto a lavadoras de carga frontal como de carga superior:
- Cajón del detergente: remojar en agua caliente con jabón para lavavajillas o vinagre, y frotar con un paño de microfibra y un cepillo de dientes para retirar la suciedad incrustada.
- Filtro de drenaje: ubicarlo generalmente en la parte inferior del equipo, retirarlo y sumergirlo en agua caliente para eliminar pelusa y restos de detergente antes de volver a colocarlo.
- Tambor: rociar con vinagre blanco y limpiar con un paño de microfibra, evitando el contacto frecuente con el empaque de goma para prevenir corrosión.
- Empaque de goma: ejecutar un ciclo en vacío con bicarbonato de sodio a 90 grados Celsius (194 grados Fahrenheit), seguido de una limpieza con agua tibia y jabón, ya que esta zona concentra buena parte de los malos olores.
- Exterior del equipo: en lavadoras de carga frontal, aplicar vinagre blanco o un spray antibacteriano, con productos específicos para acabados en acero inoxidable. En las de carga superior, utilizar el ciclo más caliente con vinagre blanco, pausar para dejar actuar la solución y finalizar con bicarbonato de sodio.
Productos y hábitos que recomiendan los fabricantes
Entre las recomendaciones adicionales que comparten las distintas marcas destacan:
- Utilizar vinagre blanco y bicarbonato de sodio como limpiadores básicos contra el moho y los olores.
- Emplear jabón para lavavajillas para atacar hongos de forma temprana.
- Evitar el uso excesivo de blanqueador, que puede dañar tanto el equipo como las prendas si no se enjuaga correctamente.
- Realizar una limpieza de rutina al menos dos veces al año.
- Revisar las configuraciones de ciclo de limpieza disponibles en cada modelo.
- Usar percarbonato de sodio como alternativa más segura frente a los malos olores.
- Combatir la cal con vinagre o pastillas específicas para prevenir daños por acumulación de sarro.
- Ventilar el tambor y el cajón del detergente de forma periódica.
Cuidados adicionales para prolongar la vida útil
Los fabricantes también insisten en tres prácticas simples que reducen la necesidad de limpiezas profundas. La primera consiste en dejar la puerta abierta después de cada lavado, para que la humedad se evapore y no favorezca la formación de moho. La segunda recomienda el uso de detergentes de alta calidad, que generan menos residuos acumulados dentro del tambor.
La tercera práctica apunta a la inspección periódica de mangueras y conexiones, con el objetivo de detectar fugas u obstrucciones antes de que generen fallas mayores en el sistema de drenaje. Según los fabricantes, la combinación de estas rutinas de limpieza y revisión permite mantener el equipo en condiciones óptimas durante más tiempo, al mismo tiempo que se reduce el riesgo de reparaciones costosas asociadas al deterioro por falta de mantenimiento.
La diferencia entre una lavadora que funciona durante años sin inconvenientes y otra que desarrolla olores, obstrucciones o fallas prematuras no depende tanto de la calidad del equipo como de la constancia en su mantenimiento. Dedicar unos minutos al mes a esta tarea representa, en definitiva, una inversión menor frente al costo y la incomodidad que implica una reparación evitable.

articles.title: Orange va déployer un câble sous-marin géant de plus de 3000 kilomètres le long de l'Europe de l'ouest
articles.text:
Un nouveau câble sous-marin important va voir le jour dans l'Atlantique, le long de l'Europe de l'ouest. Et Orange sera à la baguette.
Une des infrastructures les plus critiques aujourd'hui sur la planète sont les câbles sous-marins, qui permettent d'assurer le trafic internet. En général, ces câbles appartiennent aux géants de la tech, comme les GAFAM, ou bien à des opérateurs, comme notre Orange national. Une entreprise qui va être à l'origine d'un nouveau projet de câble.
Orange et ses partenaires vont déployer le câble Pisces, long de près de 3 125 kilomètres
Orange est partout sur les câbles sous-marins en ce moment. L'opérateur français avait déjà annoncé au mois de septembre qu'il allait tirer un câble entre la Réunion et l'Afrique du Sud. Aujourd'hui, on apprend qu'Orange va porter un autre projet de câble, celui-là dans l'océan Atlantique.
Pour ce projet, il sera accompagné de ses partenaires Equitix et MDM afin de mettre au monde un nouveau câble sous-marin du nom de Pisces. Celui-ci, long de 3 125 kilomètres, va relier l'Irlande à la France, l'Espagne et le Portugal.
Un déploiement programmé pour 2028
Plus exactement, ce câble, doté de 16 paires de fibres optiques, va partir de Galway (Irlande) pour passer par Saint-Hilaire-de Riez (France) puis Sopelana (Espagne) avant de finir à Carcavelos (Portugal). L'Union européenne va participer financièrement à ce projet, qui va notamment permettre à l'Irlande de bénéficier de liens plus directs avec le Vieux Continent, sans avoir à passer par le Royaume-Uni.
Le câble va aussi permettre d'améliorer les échanges, nombreux, entre l'Irlande, où atterrissent la majorité des câbles sous-marins traversant l'Atlantique avant de continuer vers l'Europe, et le Vieux Continent. L'Irlande est en effet un hub pour les géants du cloud - ce qui est illustré par le fait que Dublin soit la troisième région du monde avec le plus de data centers au monde, derrière la Virginie et Pékin. Le déploiement du câble Pisces aura lieu en 2028.

articles.title: ATK Introduces the Blazing Sky Phantom, a 44g Carbon-Fiber Wireless Gaming Mouse With Dual 8K Polling
articles.text:
Thursday, October 15th 2026
ATK Introduces the Blazing Sky Phantom, a 44g Carbon-Fiber Wireless Gaming Mouse With Dual 8K Polling
ATK GEAR has expanded its Blazing Sky mouse lineup with the new ATK Blazing Sky Phantom Hollow Carbon Fiber Composite Wireless Gaming Mouse, a lightweight esports-focused model built around a composite carbon-fiber shell, an open cutout structure, and ATK's latest in-house wireless performance platform. The Phantom is aimed at competitive FPS players who want a small-to-medium symmetrical shape, low click latency, and a high-end sensor package without moving into an oversized chassis.
The Phantom is available through ATK's official store.At first glance, the Phantom stands out from ATK's more conventional shells. The mouse uses a hollow carbon-fiber composite construction with staggered geometric cutouts across the body. Instead of making the weight-saving structure look purely functional, ATK has paired the cutouts with a distressed retro sunburst side print, giving the mouse a layered visual identity that looks closer to a custom enthusiast peripheral than a standard esports mouse. Four color options are listed: Prime, Dune, Verge, and Eon.
The headline number is weight. ATK lists the Blazing Sky Phantom at 44±3 g, placing it firmly in the ultralight category while retaining wireless connectivity and an internal 300 mAh battery. The dimensions are 119.7 mm × 62.5 mm × 37.3 mm, which positions it as a compact-to-mid-size option. The shape is symmetrical and relatively low-profile, with a tapered waist, centered ridge, and thumb support designed for controlled repositioning during fast aim adjustments. ATK recommends the Phantom for small-to-medium hands, with support for claw, palm, and fingertip grip styles.
Inside, the Phantom uses the PAW3955 Master sensor, a flagship-grade optical sensor configured for very fine sensitivity control. ATK lists support for up to 50,000 DPI, with 1-2 DPI step adjustment depending on configuration, and an adjustable lift-off distance range from 0.7 mm to 1.7 mm. For competitive players who tune their setup around consistent tracking and repeatable flicks, that level of granularity gives the Phantom a strong technical foundation.
The mouse is also built around ATK's self-developed ApexShark MAX Mouse Solution, using the NORDIC 54LM20 MCU and third-generation competitive firmware. According to ATK, the platform supports a static scan rate of over 20,000 FPS and enables dual 8000 Hz polling in both wired and 2.4 GHz wireless modes. The Phantom ships with support for ATK's 8K receiver ecosystem, including the GEM 8K Dongle / NANO 8K Dongle depending on configuration.
Click performance is another major selling point. The Phantom uses Omron optical switches and is rated for click latency as low as 0.174 ms. Optical switches also avoid traditional mechanical debounce behavior, helping deliver more consistent actuation over time. Combined with 8K polling, the Phantom is clearly being positioned for players who care about input responsiveness as much as raw weight.
Battery life is rated at up to 200 hours at 1000 Hz, powered by a 300 mAh high-density battery. As usual with high-polling-rate wireless mice, real-world endurance at 4000 Hz or 8000 Hz will be lower, but the 1000 Hz figure gives users flexibility when switching between competitive sessions and everyday desktop use. Connectivity includes both wired and 2.4 GHz wireless operation.
The Phantom also features ATK's all-new nano coating, a Raesha optical scroll wheel encoder, and the brand's broader software ecosystem through ATK HUB, which is designed to manage device settings, profiles, and performance tuning. ATK has increasingly positioned its peripherals as part of a connected esports hardware/software stack rather than standalone devices, and the Phantom continues that direction.
From a market perspective, the Blazing Sky Phantom enters a crowded but fast-moving category: ultra-lightweight wireless gaming mice for FPS players. Its differentiators are the carbon-fiber composite shell, distinctive hollow design, PAW3955 Master sensor, dual 8K polling, and very low quoted click latency. For players already using compact symmetrical shapes, the Phantom's 44 g target weight and small-to-medium hand tuning may be the biggest draw.
ATK GEAR says its product development is shaped by its background in gaming media, esports feedback, and hardware R&D. The company has built visibility through products such as the ATK68 magnetic keyboard, ATK F1 mouse, EDGE 60HE, and RS6 keyboards, while continuing to test and refine products with competitive teams. With the Phantom, ATK appears to be pushing further into the enthusiast FPS mouse segment with a product that emphasizes both visual design and measurable performance specifications.
The ATK Blazing Sky Phantom Hollow Carbon Fiber Composite Wireless Gaming Mouse is listed at $99.98 USD on ATK's official store at the time of writing, with a regular listed price of $119.98 USD. Availability and color options may vary by region and stock status.
