articles.title: Philips Hue et Google Home : vos ampoules vont devenir plus réactives, sans rien faire
articles.text:
Google améliore le fonctionnement des ampoules Philips Hue dans son application Maison grâce au protocole Matter. Une mise à jour automatique promet des commandes plus rapides et plus fiables, sans avoir à reconfigurer son installation.
Une ampoule connectée qui met plusieurs secondes à s'allumer, ce n'est jamais très agréable. Et lorsque la connexion Internet fait des siennes, les commandes deviennent parfois franchement capricieuses. Google entend améliorer la situation pour les utilisateurs de Philips Hue avec une mise à jour de son application Google Home. Le constructeur active désormais automatiquement le contrôle local des ponts Hue existants, en s'appuyant sur Matter. Une évolution assez discrète, mais qui pourrait rendre l'éclairage connecté plus agréable au quotidien. Le tout sans demander aux utilisateurs de toucher à leurs réglages.
Google Home passe au contrôle local des ampoules Philips Hue
Dans ses notes de mise à jour du 14 octobre, Google annonce que les installations Philips Hue équipées d'un pont compatible peuvent désormais basculer automatiquement vers le contrôle local Matter.
Concrètement, les commandes envoyées depuis Google Home peuvent transiter directement par le réseau domestique, plutôt que de dépendre systématiquement de serveurs distants. Pour allumer une ampoule, modifier sa luminosité ou changer sa couleur, ce chemin plus direct doit permettre de réduire les délais de réaction.
Google promet ainsi une meilleure réactivité et une fiabilité accrue. Le constructeur ne fournit toutefois aucune mesure permettant de quantifier ces progrès. Les bénéfices réels dépendront notamment de la configuration du réseau domestique.
L'autre avantage concerne la continuité du service. Lorsque les équipements compatibles peuvent communiquer localement, certaines commandes restent envisageables même en cas de coupure de la connexion Internet. Il ne faut cependant pas en déduire que toutes les fonctionnalités de Google Home ou de Philips Hue deviennent indépendantes du cloud.
La bonne nouvelle, c'est surtout que la transition s'effectue en arrière-plan, sans nouvel appairage. Les utilisateurs n'ont donc pas à supprimer leurs ampoules de Google Home pour les ajouter à nouveau.
Une mise à jour bienvenue pour les installations existantes
Philips Hue prend déjà en charge Matter depuis plusieurs années. Les ponts Hue Bridge et Bridge Pro permettent notamment d'intégrer les éclairages de la marque à différents écosystèmes domotiques. La nouveauté annoncée par Google concerne donc la manière dont sa plateforme communique avec ces installations, et non l'arrivée de Matter chez Philips Hue.
Un hub Google Home compatible Matter reste nécessaire pour profiter de cette évolution. Google ne précise pas quelles générations de ponts Hue sont effectivement prises en charge au-delà de sa référence générale aux modèles existants.
La mise à jour apporte également des améliorations plus larges au contrôle des appareils Matter, ainsi qu'une interface revue pour les éclairages, prises et interrupteurs connectés d'autres fabricants. Google promet notamment des réglages plus agréables pour la luminosité et les couleurs.
Concernant la disponibilité, Google ne mentionne aucune restriction géographique dans son annonce, mais ne précise pas non plus à quel moment chaque installation bénéficiera du changement. Les utilisateurs français devront donc éventuellement patienter pendant le déploiement.
Pour ceux qui possèdent déjà plusieurs ampoules Hue et un équipement Google Home compatible, l'amélioration a au moins un mérite : elle ne nécessite aucun nouvel achat ni manipulation supplémentaire. Reste à vérifier si cette optimisation sera aussi perceptible au quotidien que Google le promet.

articles.title: Bell proposes 55-metre 5G tower built on Orillia church's property
articles.text:
Bell has submitted a proposal to build a new 55-metre 5G tower in Orillia, Ont., but with a twist: it would sit on a church property.
The self-supporting tower would be built on the Calvary Pentecostal Church property at 375 Westmount Drive North, right beside Highway 11. Interestingly, it is across the street from where notable Canadian musician Gordon Lightfoot is buried.
Bell says that the new site will improve local wireless coverage, strengthen indoor cell signal, increase network capacity, deliver faster speeds, and help serve businesses and residents along the Highway 11 corridor.
The telecom giant says that the growing demand for wireless service is driving the need for additional infrastructure, and that the tower would complement the company’s existing sites in the area.
The church’s pastor told Orillia Matters that Bell first approached it about two years ago, and after consultations, the local board agreed to host the tower. Bell later offered compensation for use of the property—the amount of which has not been disclosed. Commenters on the story expressed relief at the news, with many noting that Bell has poor service in the area.
Now, this is still a proposal, and Bell is currently going through the public consultation process. Anyone can comment to consultation@canacre.com by October 30, 2026, and must use the reference number X6548.
Header image credit: Bell
Source: The City of Orillia via PlanHub

articles.title: 5 Non-fiction books you must read before 2026 ends
articles.text:
5 Non-fiction books you must read before 2026 ends
Discover five must-read nonfiction books before 2026 ends, exploring Indian politics, Kashmir, scams, archaeology and wildlife conservation.
As 2026 is about to come to a close, it is a good time to pick up books that challenge familiar ideas, uncover overlooked stories and offer a deeper understanding of the world around us.
Nonfiction can do more than share facts; it can introduce readers to unfamiliar communities, examine the forces shaping society and encourage them to question what they have long taken for granted.
From political and social realities to investigations into crime, history and the natural world, these five nonfiction books offer different ways to look beyond everyday headlines. If you want to make your reading list more thought-provoking before the year ends, these titles deserve a place on it.
1. Believer’s Dilemma by Abhishek Choudhary
Believer’s Dilemma by Abhishek Choudhary is a compelling choice for readers interested in the relationship between belief, politics and public life. The title raises questions about what happens when personal convictions meet complex political realities, making it particularly relevant to readers who enjoy examining the ideas that influence society.
Books that explore belief and ideology encourage readers to look beyond easy answers. They can help us understand how individuals reconcile their principles with the institutions, movements and circumstances around them. For readers who enjoy political nonfiction and want to examine the tensions between conviction and reality, this book is worth considering.
2. Dapaan by Ipsita Chakravarty
In Dapaan, Ipsita Chakravarty brings readers towards the social and cultural realities that often remain outside mainstream conversations. The book is a worthwhile addition for anyone interested in understanding how communities, identities and lived experiences shape the way people see the world.
One of the most valuable aspects of reading nonfiction is the opportunity to encounter perspectives that differ from our own. Stories rooted in specific places and communities can reveal how history, culture and social structures influence everyday life. Dapaan is a title to explore if you want your reading list to move beyond familiar narratives and introduce you to a different perspective on society.
3. Scamlands by Snigdha Poonam
For readers fascinated by investigations, deception and the people behind elaborate schemes, Scamlands by Snigdha Poonam is a title to add to the list. Investigative nonfiction can reveal the circumstances that allow scams to flourish, exploring the relationships between ambition, opportunity, vulnerability and trust.
Scams are not simply stories about people losing money. They can also expose weaknesses in institutions, the appeal of quick success and the ways people are persuaded to believe in promises that seem too good to be true. Reading about these patterns can encourage greater scepticism and help readers recognise the importance of questioning extraordinary claims.
If you enjoy true stories that combine investigation with insights into human behaviour, Scamlands is a strong candidate for your year-end reading list.
4. The Dig by Sowmiya Ashok
The Dig by Sowmiya Ashok offers a title worth exploring for readers drawn to investigative reporting and the process of uncovering stories beneath the surface. The very idea of a dig suggests looking deeper, examining evidence and discovering details that might otherwise remain hidden.
Good investigative nonfiction asks readers to pay attention to the questions behind the facts. It examines how evidence is gathered, how competing accounts are assessed and why certain stories take time to understand. This approach can make readers more thoughtful about the information they encounter in news reports and public discussions.
For anyone hoping to read more deeply reported nonfiction before the year ends, The Dig is another title to consider.
5. Wild Capital by Neha Sinha
In Wild Capital, Neha Sinha brings attention to the relationship between the natural world and the human systems that influence it. For readers interested in wildlife, conservation and environmental questions, the book offers an opportunity to explore the larger forces that shape how people and nature coexist.
Environmental nonfiction is especially valuable because it connects ecological concerns with questions about development, resources and the future of shared landscapes. It encourages readers to see wildlife not as something separate from human life, but as part of a wider system affected by our decisions.
If you want to broaden your understanding of conservation and the challenges facing the natural world, Wild Capital deserves consideration as part of your reading plans.
Final thoughts
A meaningful reading list does not have to focus on a single subject. The five books above span different areas of interest, from belief and society to investigative reporting and the environment. Together, they offer an opportunity to explore unfamiliar perspectives and think more critically about the world.
Before 2026 ends, consider choosing the title that most closely matches your curiosity, or challenge yourself to read all five. The best nonfiction books do more than fill your time; they leave you with new questions, fresh perspectives and ideas worth thinking about long after you finish the final page.

articles.title: Mejores enchufes inteligentes: cómo funcionan y 7 modelos recomendados para ahorrar en la factura de la luz
articles.text:
Muchas veces caemos en el error de pensar que empezar a domotizar partes de nuestra casa requiere una inversión muy elevada. Tener el control de muchos de nuestros aparatos electrónicos es más sencillo de lo que pensamos, especialmente si tenemos un enchufe inteligente. Gracias a estos, podemos ser capaces de controlar cuándo funcionan, la energía que consumen e incluso configurar rutinas. Actualmente, podemos encontrar todo tipo de modelos, pero si tuviéramos que quedarnos con uno, sin duda nos decantaríamos por el Tapo P115.
Tapo P115(1-Pack)-Enchufe Inteligente WiFi, Plug&Play, Monitoreo Energético | Programa Horarios y Temporizadores. Monitorización de Energía. Modo Ausente. Control App Tapo. Control Voz Alexa/Google.
Uno de los aspectos más destacados de este modelo es su diseño. Gracias a ese acabado cilíndrico, logra ofrecer unas dimensiones bastante más pequeñas que las de otras alternativas, lo que lo hace perfecto para colocarlo en regletas o tomas múltiples sin estorbar el resto de tomas. Además, lo hace sin hacer sacrificios en potencia, ya que admite hasta 16 A y 3.680 W, lo que permite conectarlo incluso a radiadores portátiles o electrodomésticos de la cocina.
Pero si hablamos de su punto fuerte, ese sin duda es el registro de consumo energético. Gracias a la aplicación de Tapo, podemos monitorizar en tiempo real el gasto en vatios de aquello que tengamos enchufado, consultar gráficos históricos diarios o mensuales e incluso ingresar las tarifas de electricidad por tramos horarios. Es muy completo, ya que también es compatible con el control por voz con Alexa o Google Assistant, además de integrar funciones como temporizadores con apagado automático.
Los destacados
| Modelos |  | Perfecto para ti | Lo mejor | Lo peor | Precio desde | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tapo P115 |  | Si, además de controlar el comportamiento de los aparatos, también queremos controlar el consumo. | Diseño mini que no bloquea enchufes adyacentes y monitorización de consumo muy detallada desde la app Tapo. | No incluye soporte nativo para Apple Home/Matter de serie sin puentes adicionales. | 14,99 € | 
| Tapo P100 |  | Si quieres la opción más barata y fiable para automatizar lámparas o pequeños electrodomésticos sin complicarte. | Excelente relación calidad-precio y facilidad de configuración con Alexa y Google Assistant. | No dispone de medición de consumo eléctrico y su potencia máxima soportada es inferior a la de los modelos de 16 A. | 8,99 € | 
| SONOFF S61s |  | Si necesitas máxima potencia, compatibilidad universal con Matter o uso en zonas semiexteriores/terrazas. | Certificación IP44 resistente a salpicaduras, estándar Matter (compatible con Apple Home, Alexa y Google) y aguanta electrodomésticos pesados. | Tamaño y estética algo más voluminosos. | 10,16 € | 
| Meross Enchufe Inteligente Matter |  | Si tienes kits de paneles solares de autoconsumo o buscas total integración nativa en Apple HomeKit mediante Matter. | Medición bidireccional (consumo de aparatos o producción solar) y compatibilidad directa y rápida vía Matter Simple Setup. | La app de Meross puede resultar algo menos intuitiva y pulida que la de ecosistemas como Tapo. | 14,99 € | 
| ANTELA Enchufe Inteligente 16A |  | Si quieres domotizar varias tomas de alta potencia a bajo coste dentro del ecosistema Tuya/Smart Life. | Vienen 2 unidades con soporte para 16 A (3680 W) y monitor de energía por un coste por unidad muy ajustado. | Depende de la nube de Smart Life/Tuya, sin compatibilidad con Apple HomeKit o estándar Matter. | 17,99 € | 
| Meross Enchufe Inteligente |  | Si buscas un enchufe robusto de 16 A para electrodomésticos de gran carga sin pagar el sobrecoste de Matter. | Medidor de consumo preciso, historial descargable y gran estabilidad de conexión Wi-Fi. | No es compatible de forma nativa con Apple Home (a diferencia del modelo Matter de la marca) y su chasis es algo más ancho en regletas estrechas. | 19,99 € | 
| Philips Hue Smart Plug |  | Si ya cuentas con un ecosistema de iluminación Philips Hue o buscas la máxima estabilidad que ofrece la red Zigbee. | Calidad de construcción premium, conectividad Bluetooth + Zigbee (actúa como repetidor de red de malla) y respuesta inmediata sin saturar la red Wi-Fi. | Es el modelo más caro de la comparativa, no mide consumo eléctrico y para sacarle el 100% de funciones requiere el puente Hue Bridge. | 26,90 € | 
Por qué destacan
Aunque pueden engañar, los enchufes inteligentes entrañan una serie de aspectos mucho más complejos de lo que podríamos pensar en primer lugar. No todos los enchufes de este tipo pueden servirnos para cualquier uso. Por eso, es importante tener en cuenta una serie de consideraciones previas antes de lanzarse a comprar uno de estos modelos. A continuación, repasamos las características fundamentales que hay que tener presentes.
Amperaje y potencia. Un factor fundamental es saber qué tipo de aparatos podremos conectar a estos enchufes. Para ello, es fundamental saber el amperaje máximo soportado por el enchufe inteligente y la potencia máxima que soportan. Actualmente, podemos encontrar dos estándares diferentes:
- Modelos de 10 A (hasta ~2.300 W): Están pensados para cargas ligeras o moderadas, como lámparas de pie, cargadores, altavoces, ventiladores o equipos de sonido.
- Modelos de 16 A (hasta ~3.680 W/3.840 W): Son obligatorios si vas a conectar electrodomésticos con resistencia térmica o motores exigentes (radiadores de aceite, calefactores, termos eléctricos, lavadoras, secadoras o cafeteras exprés). Un enchufe de menor potencia podría sobrecalentarse y activar sus sistemas de seguridad.
Además, otro aspecto que no todo el mundo sabe es que este tipo de enchufes requieren una toma de tierra. Es algo habitual en las casas modernas, pero en casas muy antiguas o de campo es posible que no cuenten con este tipo de instalación eléctrica.
Forma. Otro aspecto que no hay que dejar pasar por alto es el diseño del enchufe. Si queremos conectarlo a una toma normal y corriente, esto suele ser indiferente. Sin embargo, si queremos enchufarlo a una regleta o una toma múltiple de pared, lo más recomendado es optar por modelos cilíndricos o con diseños supercompactos. De este modo, evitamos que invadan el espacio del resto de tomas, bloqueando los enchufes que estén a su lado.
Protocolo de conectividad. Para saber si seremos capaces de controlar correctamente el enchufe, es importante saber el protocolo de conectividad que utiliza. El más recomendado es que sea a través del Wi-Fi clásico con la banda de 2,4 GHz. Con él, el enchufe se vincula directamente al router, sin tener que realizar ningún paso adicional. No obstante, el inconveniente que tiene es que, si tenemos muchos enchufes de este tipo, pueden acabar saturando la red.
Luego encontramos otros protocolos como Matter o Zigbee. El primero de ellos también es bastante recomendable, ya que es el nuevo estándar para dispositivos de hogar conectado. Son compatibles con Alexa, Google Home, Apple Home o Samsung SmartThings indistintamente, eliminando las barreras concretas de cada marca. En cuanto a Zigbee, este cuenta con el inconveniente de que suelen requerir un concentrador o puente de enlace. Esto requiere una mayor inversión, pero a cambio ofrece un rendimiento inmediato, libera la red Wi-Fi y los enchufes actúan incluso como nodos repetidores, ampliando la red de casa.
Asistentes. Como acabamos de ver, este tipo de enchufes son compatibles con asistentes del hogar como Alexa, Google Home o Apple Home, entre otros. A la hora de escoger un enchufe u otro, es fundamental tener en consideración si tenemos algún dispositivo con cualquiera de estos asistentes. Es decir, si tenemos un Echo Dot de Amazon, lo recomendable es apostar por un modelo compatible con Alexa. De este modo, podremos crear un hogar interconectado con todos los dispositivos.
Seguridad. Es imprescindible revisar que el enchufe inteligente que escojamos esté fabricado con materiales ignífugos certificados, como el grado V-0, así como con mecanismos de desconexión automática por sobretensión o sobrecalentamiento. De este modo, podremos asegurarnos de que la integridad del enchufe esté garantizada, evitando la aparición de cortocircuitos.
Otras opciones a considerar
Tapo P100. Este modelo es la puerta de entrada más asequible y contrastada al ecosistema domótico de TP-Link. Su diseño cuadrado lo hace ideal para enchufes de pared, aunque no tan recomendado para el caso de usarlo en una regleta. Funciona mediante Wi-Fi directo de 2,4 GHz, por lo que su configuración es facilísima.
Está pensado para la automatización básica de pequeños aparatos, como lámparas auxiliares, ventiladores o cargadores. Dispone de programación de horarios, cuentas regresivas y creación de escenas personalizadas. Además, es compatible con el control por voz con Alexa y Google Home.
Tapo P100 - Enchufe Inteligente WiFi, Programa Horarios, Control App/Voz | Programa Horarios y Temporizadores. Modo Ausente. Control App Tapo. Control Voz Alexa/Google. Fácil Configuración.
SONOFF S61s. Aunque su precio puede engañar, el SONOFF S61s es un enchufe inteligente todoterreno, ofreciendo incluso resistencia al agua y polvo con certificación IP44. Gracias a esta protección, resulta idóneo tanto para el interior del hogar como para zonas semiexteriores, patios, terrazas cubiertas o salas de calderas. Soporta una potencia punta de hasta 16 A (3.840 W), por lo que podemos usarlo con cualquier electrodoméstico.
En el apartado de conectividad, destaca por adoptar el estándar abierto Matter, lo que garantiza una integración nativa e instantánea con servicios como los de Apple, Alexa o Google. Asimismo, incorpora un módulo de medición de energía detallado y sistemas de corte automático ante sobrecargas térmicas o de voltaje. Además, ofrece funciones como la programación de temporizador o el control por voz.
SONOFF S61s Tomada Inteligente WiFi 16A/3840W – Control Remoto & Voz, Medidor de Consumo Eléctrico, Temporizador, Compatible Matter con Alexa, Google y Apple Home
Meross Enchufe Inteligente Matter (MSS315). El aspecto más destacado de este modelo de la marca Meross es su compatibilidad con el estándar Matter. Gracias a esto, será totalmente compatible con cualquier dispositivo, funcionando a través de la red local y garantizando un rendimiento inmediato. Es compatible con el control por voz y con la creación de horarios y rutinas.
Sin embargo, este modelo destaca por la capacidad de medición bidireccional. No solo registra el consumo en tiempo real de los aparatos que enchufas, sino que también es capaz de monitorizar la generación de microplantas solares de balcón o kits fotovoltaicos de autoconsumo. Además, su aplicación recopila estadísticas de vatios y kilovatios-hora, por lo que es ideal si tenemos este tipo de placas o kits.
Meross Enchufe Inteligente Matter con Consumo de Energía, WiFi Enchufe con Matter Simple Setup(MSS), Mide Producción de Paneles Solares Fotovoltaicos, Compatible con Alexa, Apple Home y Google Home
ANTELA Enchufe Inteligente 16A (Pack 2). Este conjunto de enchufes de ANTELA es una opción muy interesante si queremos tener más de un dispositivo conectado desde el principio. Cada uno de ellos soporta cargas de hasta 16 A (3.680 W) y están fabricados con materiales ignífugos de grado V-0. Se conectan directamente a la red Wi-Fi de 2,4 GHz sin requerir pasarelas adicionales.
El ecosistema que gestiona estos dispositivos es Smart Life/Tuya Smart, dos de las plataformas domóticas más populares y compatibles del mercado. Desde la aplicación es posible consultar el consumo eléctrico acumulado en tiempo real, programar encendidos según variables climáticas o de ubicación y enlazar el dispositivo de manera fluida con los comandos de voz de Alexa y Google Home.
ANTELA Enchufe Inteligente 16A 3680W Con Monitor de Consumo, Compatible con Alexa y Google Home, 2 PCS
Meross Enchufe Inteligente 16A (Versión Wi-Fi clásica). La versión tradicional de Meross de 16 A y 3.680 W está más pensada para los que quieren tener un control minucioso de su gasto. Esto es posible gracias al chip de medición energética que incorpora, el cual es capaz de registrar el historial de consumo diario, semanal y mensual con posibilidad de exportar dichos registros.
Su chasis presenta un indicador LED discreto y un botón de encendido físico lateral, pensado para instalarse en tomas individuales. Además, este enchufe permite configurar rutinas de amanecer/anochecer, temporizadores de seguridad y control por voz mediante los asistentes principales, conectándose a través de Wi-Fi.
Meross Enchufe Inteligente con Monitor de Energía 16A con Mide el Consumo | WiFi Enchufe Alexa con Control Remoto y por Voz, Temporizador, Smart Plug Compatible con Alexa, Google Home y SmartThings
Philips Hue Smart Plug. El enchufe inteligente de Philips Hue es la opción perfecta para aquellos que tengan dispositivos de la marca. Es compatible con la conectividad dual Zigbee y Bluetooth. Esto permite vincularlo directamente al smartphone por Bluetooth o sumarse a un puente Hue Bridge para desbloquear todas las opciones que ofrece la red mallada Zigbee, garantizando que el encendido sea instantáneo y sin sobrecargar la red de nuestro hogar.
Al actuar dentro de la red Hue, este enchufe funciona además como repetidor de señal Zigbee, ampliando el rango de cobertura hacia otros accesorios de nuestra casa. Aunque prescinde de la función de medidor de vatios, su valor principal reside en convertir cualquier lámpara convencional en un modelo inteligente integrado en el ecosistema de Philips Hue.
Philips Hue Smart Plug, Tipo G, Blanco | Control Inteligente para Lámparas Estándar, Control con Aplicación Bluetooth, Funciona con Alexa, Google Home y Apple Home
Configuraciones y extras
Aunque las características que mencionábamos anteriormente son las más importantes, también hay ciertos añadidos que pueden mejorar la experiencia. Especialmente si buscamos el enchufe más completo de todos. Entre algunos de los extras que podemos valorar, nosotros destacamos los siguientes.
Monitorización de consumo. Algunos enchufes inteligentes son capaces de ofrecernos registros detallados del consumo diario, semanal, mensual y anual de nuestros dispositivos. Incluso algunos son capaces de ofrecer esta monitorización en tiempo real, para que podamos controlar al máximo el consumo que tendremos a final de mes.
Modo ausente. Hay modelos que cuentan con este modo, que permite que la aplicación directamente encienda y apague luces de nuestra casa de manera aleatoria en determinados momentos del día. De este modo, parece que hay alguien en casa, por lo que sirve para evitar que alguien ajeno entre en nuestro hogar al ver que pasamos demasiados días fuera de él.
Packs. Si tenemos pensado utilizar este tipo de enchufes con varios de nuestros dispositivos o electrodomésticos, lo más recomendable es optar por la compra de packs. La mayoría de marcas ofrecen la opción de adquirir más de un enchufe de forma simultánea y, como decimos, suelen ofrecer precios más atractivos que adquirirlos por separado.
Preguntas frecuentes
¿Sirve un enchufe inteligente para cualquier electrodoméstico?
No para todos. Funcionan a la perfección con aparatos que tienen un interruptor mecánico de encendido/apagado (como lámparas de mesa, ventiladores tradicionales, radiadores analógicos o cafeteras de goteo clásicas). Sin embargo, si un aparato utiliza un botón electrónico o táctil y entra en modo de reposo al recibir corriente (por ejemplo, muchos microondas modernos, televisores o lavadoras con panel digital), el enchufe inteligente solo podrá cortar o suministrar electricidad, pero requerirá pulsar el botón manualmente para que empiece a funcionar.
¿Cuánta electricidad consume el propio enchufe inteligente?
El consumo propio del dispositivo es residual. Al mantenerse conectado a la red Wi-Fi o Zigbee en espera de órdenes, suele consumir entre 0,5 W y 1,5 W por hora. A lo largo de todo un año, esto se traduce en un coste aproximado de entre 1 y 2 euros, una cifra que queda holgadamente compensada al eliminar el consumo en reposo de los equipos que apaga por completo.
¿Qué pasa si se va la luz o se corta internet?
- Si se va la luz: Al volver el suministro, la mayoría de los modelos permiten configurar a través de su app el "estado tras corte eléctrico": puedes elegir si prefieres que se quede apagado, encendido o que recuerde el estado exacto en el que estaba antes del apagón.
- Si se cae la conexión a internet: No podrás controlarlo desde fuera de casa ni por voz mediante Alexa o Google Assistant. No obstante, las programaciones y temporizadores guardados en la memoria interna del enchufe seguirán ejecutándose con normalidad, y muchos modelos permiten el control manual directo mediante el botón físico de la carcasa o el control local a través de la red doméstica (especialmente en dispositivos con Matter o Zigbee).
¿Es seguro conectar aparatos de gran potencia como radiadores o termos?
Sí, siempre y cuando el enchufe cuente con una capacidad de 16 A (hasta 3.680 W) y disponga de protecciones térmicas y contra sobrecargas. Es fundamental no utilizar enchufes básicos de 10 A (diseñados solo para un máximo de ~2.300 W) con aparatos de resistencia eléctrica continua, ya que podrían sobrecalentarse y provocar problemas en la instalación.
¿Por qué la mayoría de enchufes Wi-Fi solo funcionan en redes de 2,4 GHz?
La banda de 2,4 GHz ofrece un alcance mucho mayor y una mejor capacidad para atravesar paredes y obstáculos que la de 5 GHz, lo cual resulta ideal para accesorios del hogar conectado que envían paquetes de datos muy ligeros. Si tu router emite ambas frecuencias bajo el mismo nombre (red mixta), es habitual tener que desactivar temporalmente la red de 5 GHz durante la vinculación inicial para que el móvil y el enchufe se sincronicen sin errores.
¿Se pueden colocar enchufes inteligentes en exteriores o cuartos húmedos?
Solo aquellos modelos que cuenten con certificación específica contra agua y polvo (mínimo IP44 para zonas bajo techo o terrazas protegidas, o IP65/IP66 para intemperie total). Conectar un enchufe convencional de interior en un jardín, terraza descubierta o baño expuesto a humedad directa supone un riesgo de cortocircuito.
¿Cómo ayuda un enchufe inteligente a ahorrar en la factura eléctrica?
Permite el ahorro a través de tres vías principales:
- Detección de consumos fantasma: Identifica qué electrodomésticos siguen gastando electricidad incluso apagados y automatiza su desconexión total.
- Programación por tramos horarios: Automatiza la puesta en marcha de acumuladores, termos eléctricos o deshumidificadores durante las horas valle (cuando el precio del kilovatio-hora es más económico).
- Apagados automáticos: Evita descuidos mediante temporizadores que desconectan radiadores o cargadores tras un tiempo límite establecido.
Recomendación final
En el caso de que estés buscando un enchufe inteligente compatible con cualquier dispositivo o electrodoméstico, tenemos claro que el Tapo P115 es la mejor opción. Tiene la potencia suficiente para ello, y gracias a su diseño cilíndrico, no deberíamos preocuparnos de que acabe robándole espacio a otras tomas de nuestras regletas o enchufes.
Es capaz de monitorizar el consumo eléctrico y de establecer diferentes programas horarios gracias a la aplicación de Tapo. Además, es compatible con Alexa o Google Home e incluye añadidos tan interesantes como el modo ausente. Para un enchufe inteligente para casa, es un acierto total.
Tapo P115(1-Pack)-Enchufe Inteligente WiFi, Plug&Play, Monitoreo Energético | Programa Horarios y Temporizadores. Monitorización de Energía. Modo Ausente. Control App Tapo. Control Voz Alexa/Google.
En el caso de que queramos algo más orientado a zonas exteriores semicubiertas, el SONOFF S61s es una alternativa fantástica. Prácticamente comparte las características más importantes del Tapo P115, pero con el añadido de que cuenta con certificación IP44 contra polvo y salpicaduras. Por tanto, podemos colocarlo fuera de casa sin demasiado temor.

articles.title: Xreal dévoile les 1 Pro+, des lunettes connectées qui transforment la 2D en 3D
articles.text:
Après les Xreal 1 Pro, sorties en décembre 2024, le constructeur chinois Xreal est de retour avec une nouvelle paire de lunettes connectées : les Xreal 1 Pro+. Celles-ci intègrent une technologie permettant de transformer des contenus 2D en contenus 3D, et un traitement HDR par IA. Spécificités, prix, date de lancement : voici tout ce qu’il faut savoir.
Un écran micro-OLED, de la 3D et du HDR par IA
Les Xreal 1 Pro+ intègrent un écran Sony Micro-OLED de 0,55 pouce, affichant une définition de 1 920 × 1 080 pixels par œil. Elles offrent un champ de vision de 57° et une luminosité perçue pouvant atteindre 1 200 nits. Grâce à la puce X1, développée par Xreal, ces lunettes connectées prennent en charge la conversion native des contenus 2D en 3D jusqu’à 60 Hz. Aucun matériel ni logiciel supplémentaire n’est nécessaire, il suffit de connecter les lunettes à une source vidéo (ordinateur, téléphone…). Notons également l’intégration d’une technologie 3DoF native qui permet de maintenir l’écran virtuel à une position fixe dans l’espace, même lorsque l’utilisateur bouge la tête.
Associées à l’accessoire optionnel Xreal Eye, les Xreal 1 Pro+ prennent en charge le suivi des mouvements dans l’espace sur six degrés de liberté (6DoF) ainsi que les interactions gestuelles. Ces fonctionnalités permettent d’interagir plus naturellement avec les éléments virtuels.
Elles intègrent également un traitement HDR par IA qui « optimise intelligemment les hautes lumières, les ombres, les tons de peau, les sous-titres et les détails de l’image, afin de rendre les contenus du quotidien plus riches, plus nets et plus tridimensionnels », selon Xreal. Trois modes d’affichage sont par ailleurs proposés : Lecture, Film et Standard, ainsi qu’un système d’assombrissement électrochromique. La partie audio est quant à elle assurée par nul autre que Bose, mais le constructeur ne donne pas plus de précisions à ce sujet.
Enfin, notons que Xreal promet un confort optimal lorsque ces lunettes connectées sont portées, notamment grâce à une nouvelle plaquette nasale repensée pour mieux convenir aux arêtes nasales plus hautes, ce qui devrait offrir « un meilleur ajustement à davantage d’utilisateurs, notamment aux personnes présentant des morphologies faciales occidentales ».
Prix et date de lancement
Les Xreal 1 Pro+ sont disponibles dès ce 15 octobre 2026 sur la boutique officielle du constructeur, au prix de 649 €. Elles seront également proposées sur Amazon fin octobre, sans date précise pour le moment. Le fabricant proposera également un pack à 648 dollars, comprenant les lunettes et la caméra Xreal Eye.

articles.title: Nvidia and Cisco unveil next-gen network interface built for the AI data center boom
articles.text:
In Layman's Terms: New data center projects are emerging everywhere, with no end in sight. Traditional data center interconnects are becoming increasingly inefficient, which is why Nvidia and Cisco have developed a new standard designed to move all those terabytes of data as quickly and efficiently as possible.
GPU maker Nvidia and networking specialist Cisco have unveiled a new network interface called Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable (USFP). The new optical transceiver is designed to significantly increase bandwidth in data centers, helping accommodate the enormous data demands of modern AI models and training workloads.
The USFP module is the first interface to support 400Gb/s per lane, Cisco said. Ultimately, the module is expected to support total data transfer rates of up to 12.8Tb/s. USFP's total bandwidth capacity is four times that of optical interfaces offering 200Gb/s per lane, while also delivering a 1.3x improvement in power efficiency.
Cisco said USFP is designed to give data center customers access to next-generation optical networking technology that can accommodate the growth of their AI projects. The new interface is intended to scale efficiently using an established deployment model, although several development steps remain before it reaches the full 12.8Tb/s capacity envisioned by its designers.
The first USFP-based optical transceivers are expected to feature 16 full-duplex lanes in an octal small form factor footprint. These pluggable interfaces will support both switches and SuperNIC network adapters. The latter are specialized accelerator cards designed by Nvidia and its partners to move data directly between GPUs using the RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCE) network protocol. Put simply, RoCE enables remote direct memory access over Ethernet networks.
The next phase will expand the number of lanes to 32 or more, potentially allowing AI networking systems to connect additional 1.6Tb/s endpoints without adding more network tiers. Cisco expects the complete USFP module to eventually achieve an overall bandwidth capacity of 12.8Tb/s.
The company also highlights USFP's two-step insertion design, which is intended to improve signal integrity and reduce contact wear. The interface is designed to support power dissipation of up to 100 watts without requiring a dedicated cooling circuit inside the transceiver.
After developing USFP technology, Nvidia and Cisco began working with TE Connectivity and Amphenol to create the remaining components of the new networking infrastructure. Third-party companies are making cages, connectors, and modules for the USFP interface, and more partners are expected to join the effort.
New data center projects are adopting various networking solutions to handle their massive AI workloads. Cisco acknowledged that pluggable modules such as USFP will form part of a broader ecosystem that includes near-packaged, co-packaged, and other emerging optical architectures. These silicon photonics technologies could continue to deliver significant benefits to the data center market even if the AI bubble eventually bursts.

articles.title: LibreOffice oferece alternativa grátis após fim do Microsoft Publisher • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
LibreOffice oferece alternativa grátis após fim do Microsoft Publisher
Draw permite importar e editar documentos PUB, com opção de salvar em formato aberto.
A The Document Foundation, responsável pelo LibreOffice, sugere o uso da sua suíte gratuita como alternativa para quem ainda precisa acessar arquivos do Microsoft Publisher após o encerramento do aplicativo.
O Publisher foi descontinuado neste mês e era voltado à criação de folhetos, boletins, cartazes, cartões e outros materiais com diagramação. Seu fim afeta diretamente o acesso pelo Microsoft 365. Usuários com licença permanente ainda podem utilizar o programa sem o suporte oficial.
A entidade destaca que o Draw permite abrir e editar documentos com extensão “.pub”. Em publicação divulgada nesta quarta-feira (14/10), a fundação indica que o caminho é importar o documento no aplicativo destinado a desenhos e organização de elementos gráficos. Depois, o usuário pode salvar uma cópia editável em formato OpenDocument Drawing, com extensão “.odg”, ou exportar o resultado para PDF.
Isso permite que outros programas leiam os documentos sem depender do aplicativo original da Microsoft. O suporte já existia bem antes da aposentadoria do Publisher. O LibreOffice 4.0, lançado em fevereiro de 2013, já conseguia ler esses arquivos. O anúncio desta semana só reforça essa possibilidade.
A própria fundação reconhece que o Draw não é um aplicativo dedicado à editoração pesada, mas o indica para documentos pequenos, como boletins, ou materiais de página única. O Scribus, programa aberto voltado à editoração, também é citado como alternativa para importar arquivos do Publisher.
A Microsoft começou a exibir avisos de descontinuação do Publisher antes do encerramento. Na página de suporte, a empresa distingue o impacto sobre assinantes do Microsoft 365 e usuários que compraram uma licença permanente.
Para o Microsoft 365, o cronograma estabeleceu a perda de acesso em 1º de outubro de 2026 ou pouco depois. Já o suporte da versão permanente terminou em 13 de outubro, junto do Office 2021 e do Office LTSC 2021. A Microsoft esclarece que essa edição pode continuar sendo instalada e utilizada, inclusive para acessar e modificar arquivos existentes.
Antes da retirada, a Microsoft recomendava converter os documentos para PDF. Para editar o conteúdo no Word, a orientação era abrir esse PDF no processador de textos. A empresa também sugere Word e PowerPoint para tarefas comuns antes realizadas no Publisher, mas alerta que a conversão pode alterar a disposição dos elementos, especialmente quando há muitas imagens.
Vale lembrar que a The Document Foundation já havia criticado a Microsoft por dificuldades de compatibilidade com formatos do Office. O LibreOffice está disponível gratuitamente no site oficial para Windows, macOS e Linux.

articles.title: Plex now helps sell movie theater tickets
articles.text:
Plex, which made a name for itself by letting users share movies they own, is now helping sell movie theater tickets. The company is looking to monetize its content-discovery capabilities and expand its business beyond its media server software.
Plex partnered with Fandango, which has sold movie tickets since 2000, to drive ticket sales from people searching for movies to stream. Per the announcement:
Starting today, Plex users in the US will see a Fandango ticketing option on title pages for movies currently playing in theaters, allowing them to click through to Fandango to find showtimes and purchase tickets. The integration also enables direct attribution through Kochava, giving studios and advertisers greater visibility into how campaigns and audience engagement translate into ticket sales.
Fandango says it sells tickets for 31,000 movie theater screens in the US. The Plex deal allows it to leverage data from Plex’s streaming service (Plex claims users of the service “make more than 100 million streaming decisions each month”), including “ratings and cross-platform viewing” to gain “insight into audience intent,” the announcement said.
“Plex has a unique view into what movie fans are actively considering, from what they’re searching for to what they’re watching across services,” Jerramy Hainline, executive vice president at Fandango, said in a statement. “By connecting those discovery signals with Fandango ticketing, we’re making it easier for fans to turn that interest into a trip to the theater, while giving studios and advertisers a more direct, measurable path to ticket sales.”

articles.title: Juegos gratis de PS Plus Extra para octubre de 2026: Mafia: The Old Country encabeza la lista
articles.text:
PlayStation Plus suma nueve juegos a los catálogos Extra y Premium, denominado Deluxe en América Latina, durante octubre de 2026. La actualización incluye el estreno de Mafia: The Old Country, el regreso de Horizon Forbidden West y la incorporación desde el primer día de Mycopunk.
Los títulos se integrarán de manera escalonada. La mayor parte del catálogo estará disponible el 20 de octubre, aunque algunos lanzamientos tienen fechas específicas para Estados Unidos, Reino Unido y Japón. Los usuarios con suscripción Extra podrán acceder a siete juegos, mientras que Premium o Deluxe agregará dos títulos al catálogo de clásicos.
PlayStation Plus Extra y Premium o Deluxe permiten descargar o acceder a una selección rotativa de juegos mientras la suscripción esté activa y los títulos permanezcan en el catálogo.
Cuáles son los juegos que llegán a PlayStation Plus Extra
- Mafia: The Old Country
El principal estreno de la actualización es Mafia: The Old Country, disponible en PS5. El juego traslada la acción a la Sicilia de comienzos del siglo XX y sitúa al jugador en los orígenes del crimen organizado.
La historia sigue a Enzo Fava, quien busca demostrar su valor para una familia mafiosa en un periodo atravesado por ajustes de cuentas, redes de extorsión y enfrentamientos armados. La aventura transcurre en tercera persona y presenta vehículos de época, desplazamientos a caballo y escenarios rurales.
El uso del estilete y de la escopeta recortada lupara forma parte del arsenal y del ambiente que rodea a Enzo. La propuesta se concentra en el ascenso del protagonista dentro de un submundo criminal que domina buena parte de la vida local.
Mafia: The Old Country llegará al catálogo de PS Plus Extra el 20 de octubre.
- Horizon Forbidden West
La otra incorporación central es Horizon Forbidden West, que vuelve a PlayStation Plus para PS5 y PS4. El juego permite acompañar otra vez a Aloy en su viaje por el Oeste Prohibido, una región donde conviven máquinas de gran tamaño, ruinas del pasado y facciones enfrentadas.
La protagonista deberá recorrer territorios alejados, reunirse con viejos aliados y establecer acuerdos con nuevos grupos. La trama mantiene como eje el legado de una civilización anterior y la aparición de una amenaza que parece imposible de detener.
El juego combina combates contra criaturas mecánicas con el recorrido de paisajes posapocalípticos. Aloy debe mantenerse un paso delante de ese nuevo enemigo mientras busca respuestas sobre el pasado y el futuro de su mundo.
Horizon Forbidden West estará disponible desde el 20 de octubre para los miembros de PS Plus Extra.
La lista completa de juegos de PS Plus Extra
La actualización de octubre reúne siete títulos para el plan Extra. El calendario contempla una llegada anticipada, tres incorporaciones el 20 de octubre y otros tres lanzamientos con una fecha posterior en algunos mercados.
- The Midnight Walk | PS5: disponible el 14 de octubre en Estados Unidos y Reino Unido, y el 15 de octubre en Japón.
- Mafia: The Old Country | PS5: disponible el 20 de octubre.
- Mycopunk | PS5: disponible el 20 de octubre.
- Horizon Forbidden West | PS5 y PS4: disponible el 20 de octubre.
- Poppy Playtime: Chapter 2 | PS5 y PS4: disponible el 27 de octubre en Estados Unidos, Reino Unido y Japón.
- Tales of Arise – Beyond the Dawn Edition | PS5 y PS4: disponible el 27 de octubre en Estados Unidos, Reino Unido y Japón.
- Monster Energy Supercross 25 – The Official Video Game | PS5: disponible el 27 de octubre en Estados Unidos, Reino Unido y Japón.
Mycopunk llega desde el primer día a PlayStation Plus. El juego propone partidas cooperativas de hasta cuatro personas y pone al jugador al frente de un grupo de robots contratados por la corporación SAXON para investigar una catástrofe fúngica en un planeta.
Los juegos clásicos que llegan a Premium o Deluxe
Los miembros de PlayStation Plus Premium o Deluxe recibirán dos juegos adicionales en el catálogo de clásicos. Ambos estarán disponibles en PS5 y PS4 desde el 20 de octubre, salvo cambios regionales informados en PlayStation Store.
- Dino Crisis 2 | PS5 y PS4.
- RollerCoaster Tycoon 3 Complete Edition | PS5 y PS4.
En Dino Crisis 2, la agente Regina vuelve un año después de los acontecimientos de la operación para rescatar al doctor Kirk. Una catástrofe temporal hace desaparecer el centro de investigación de Edward City, vinculado al proyecto Tercera Energía.
RollerCoaster Tycoon 3 Complete Edition propone crear y administrar un parque de diversiones. El jugador controla finanzas, comercios, servicios y personal, con escenarios que exigen mantener satisfechos a los visitantes o un modo sandbox sin restricciones económicas.

articles.title: Even Benchmark thinks AI is eroding the venture pact against backing rivals | TechCrunch
articles.text:
For decades, the unwritten rule of venture capital was that a firm doesn’t back two companies that compete head-on. But speaking at TechCrunch Disrupt earlier this week, the partners of Benchmark readily acknowledged that the AI boom is straining that rule.
It’s been on the verge of snapping for some time. The towering AI labs OpenAI and Anthropic share dozens of the same investors at this point. Then, at the end of September, Factory, a startup that builds an AI agent to write software, said it was firing board observer and adviser Chris Degnan for “unethical conduct involving Cognition,” its direct rival and the maker of the Devin coding agent. Factory’s CEO alleged Degnan had discussed a job at Cognition while privy to Factory’s board-level discussions. Degnan said he had already resigned and denied sharing anything confidential. Soon after, he announced he was joining Cognition as chief revenue officer. Powerhouse investor Vinod Khosla sided with Degnan on X, blasting Factory’s CEO and calling the company “a struggling second tier competitor.” Khosla Ventures backs both companies.
Even Benchmark, a firm whose reputation rests on 10-to-15-year partnerships with founders at the earliest stage, said the old rule can no longer be counted on. Asked at Disrupt whether the pact against backing rivals still holds as portfolio companies expand into each other’s territory, its partners described the conflicts as a matter of necessity, not preference.
“The harsh reality of this world is every company is evolving very quickly,” said Eric Vishria. Companies pivot and change, he said, and “you are going to get conflicts, and that’s just the reality of the current dynamic.”
Vishria said Benchmark stays committed to each founder and keeps what it learns confidential, and he downplayed how much a VC could pass along anyway: “We are not product or technology experts.” Seemingly referring to the Factory-Cognition dispute, he said Benchmark has been fortunate not to land in “that type of insane direct conflict.” Exclusivity, he said, remains “really important” at the very early stage Benchmark favors. “But things are evolving. There’s no doubt about that.”
Chetan Puttagunta said AI is accelerating the problem. As the cost of building software “effectively goes to zero,” he said, founders are “incredibly ambitious.” Because they now see a “surface area” and want to claim all of it, he continued, “[i]t’s probably going to happen more, where you start to run into each other.”
He drew a line between a direct competitor at the outset, which he called “an easy answer,” and a portfolio company that expands into another’s turf over time. “That happens,” he said.
Peter Fenton called the issue “kryptonite” and the firm’s toughest problem. He described a spectrum of how investors relate to their companies. At one end is the co-founder, who would never work on a competing company. At the other is the public-market stock picker, who can own several rivals because he is merely allocating capital, not shaping any of them. Benchmark sits nearer the co-founder end, Fenton said, and treats transparency as a golden rule. “There shouldn’t be the surprise after the fact.” If a conflict does emerge, a founder should never feel shortchanged, he added.
Benchmark isn’t declaring the pact dead. At the same time, when a firm that built its name on loyalty says conflicts are coming, founders might rightly wonder who else will be this candid.

articles.title: Ugreen's NASync IDX6011 Pro finally brought my creative team together
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
This NAS definitely isn't for everybody, but if you're the kind of person who has a lot of storage (especially creative files where there may be duplicates), or you have a hard time managing all of what's there and would like some AI assistance, then this might just be the one for you. It has incredible computing power once the data is on the device, and the onboard intelligence makes managing duplicates and similar files easy. Not to mention, the built-in card readers and incredible transfer speeds make ingesting and working with the files a breeze.
Reasons to buy
- + Workstation-grade components
- + Fantastic storage capabilities
- + AI Tooling onboard
- + Editing Speeds
- + Tool-less drive settings
Reasons to avoid
- - On-Device AI could use more polish
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
I've worked with many NAS systems over the years. I have far more storage than I know what to do with at this point across the companies I work with outside my journalistic work. I've got well over a dozen active NAS systems set up, running different areas at any given time.
One branch of what I do is overseeing a photo, video, graphics, and media team. Right now, that is three people, and they have a data warehouse of sorts for their content library that I believe is around 68 TB. The majority of it is stored in Google Drive. When they are editing the files, they obviously cannot pull from Google Drive.
I have been trying to come up with a solution for a while: how I can sync down enough so they have what they need at their fingertips, without downloading 68 TB of storage onto hard drives that could fail. With storage prices rising, I didn't want to buy SSDs or redundancies.
That's when I saw this NAS announced. I was absolutely floored and unbelievably excited, especially because another growing issue was that we knew we had duplicate files. We just didn't have the time or patience to go through and manage it all.
I've had this NAS up and running for 164 days at the time of writing this. Yes, that's a long time, but I also wanted to make sure it was as stable as I thought before I put my stamp of approval on it.
Ugreen NASync IDX6011 Pro: Price and Availability
This powerhouse originally launched on Kickstarter, and is now available direct from Ugreen's website.
Prices vary depending on the configuration you choose, with my review unit costing around $2,600 with the specs I have.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Ugreen NASync IDX6011 Pro: Unboxing and First Impressions
Out of the box, this is a fantastic unboxing experience. The unit itself is very well built, so much so that even the drive trays are toolless. The trays slide out, and unlike others, where you have to pop out some side pieces to be able to mount your drives, these drives slide apart. The housing fits the drives and then snaps back into place, holding them steady.
Once I got all my drives installed, I was able to plug in power and network and get set up fairly quickly. Because I have access to it, I also plugged in the HDMI to be able to see what was on screen, but really, all it did was point me towards using the network to finish setting everything up.
I also realized during the setup process that there is a companion app that allows me to manage almost everything I would need from that app as well, more than I've seen with other tools. I can set new users, change passwords, and see status all from my phone, which is spectacular, especially if you're the kind of person who has their entire business running on this.
Ugreen NASync IDX6011 Pro: Design and Build Quality
The design and build quality of this unit is also truly great. It's sharp and professional-looking, which I appreciate. Some NAS units have gone down the line of looking friendlier, more playful, or like a home server, and I appreciate that Ugreen has kept this one professional. That's partly due to the aluminum chassis and partly to the built-in screen. Regardless, I love the look of this storage device.
Another thing worth mentioning is that even the M.2 access panel is easy to reach. Granted, it does require a hex key, but that's not the end of the world. It is still very easy to wake up.
Moving back to the front of the device, the onboard screen is very handy for checking storage, heat, and transfer speeds. Anyone who's having a nice clock on for something cool to look at.
At the back, magnetic dust filters help keep things tidy.
Ugreen NASync IDX6011 Pro: In use
Utilizing this NAS server over the last 160 days has been everything I hoped it would be... Almost. I've been able to set up Google Drive syncs. I've been able to connect four different computers via a network switch to these drives, pull content off them, and even edit the media files stored there.
That's right: I have someone editing 6K content, pulling from media files on this drive and editing them in DaVinci Resolve. I've also been able to use the AI feature to deduplicate terabytes of storage, which has been incredibly helpful and something I never would have had time to do on my own.
I've also been able to set up automatic ingestion for when people plug in SD cards, or in my team's case, Samsung T7 drives from many of the cameras that record video. This automatically dumps to one folder that then any of my team can pull up on their computer to process before saving, archiving, or deleting.
One big bummer is that, right now, Ugreen cannot sync with Google Drive shared drives. I've talked to them about this multiple times, and I believe it will be coming down the line.
Ugreen NASync IDX6011 Pro: Final verdict
At the end of the day, I don't know of any other device that can do this and run this workload for me the way this one does. Its AI deduplication feature has freed up terabytes of space.
I've been able to empower my editors to run multiple streams of video editing. I'm able to have terabytes and terabytes of storage space, fast enough computing power to be able to actually be helpful instead of just giant storage pay, but actually a media server of sorts to be able to house and be a key player in data management.
I've solved an ingest problem: previously, my users had to log in to ingest data on their computers, but now they can just plug in and go. All that's possible with the UGREEN AI NAS. I've tested it here, and it's empowered me to do all of this from the comfort of my phone for 90% of my administrative tasks, which is a huge added benefit.
If you are in the creative space or a small business and you're looking for an app that can solve a lot of problems, not just store files, this is absolutely worth checking out. However, if you don't need most of the features I mentioned above, this is 100% overkill and not worth spending money on.
For more storage solutions, we've tested out the best NAS hard drives.
Former TechRadar Pro B2B Hardware Editor, Collin has been in journalism for years, with experience in small and large markets, including Gearadical, DailyBeast, FutureNet, and more.

articles.title: Agentic workflows make speed a requirement, says Cerebras - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Cerebras positions inference speed as a competitive edge in agentic AI
Agentic workflows are making speed a condition for whole classes of AI applications to exist, and the fastest tokens will determine which platforms win the next phase of AI.
Cerebras Systems Inc., which raised $5.5 billion in its May 2026 initial public offering, built its business on making processors much faster, according to Andy Hock (pictured), chief strategy officer of Cerebras.
“We didn’t build it big because big looks cool. We built it big because AI wants big chips,” Hock said. “AI needs a lot of compute, but it needs that compute to be close together, and it also needs that compute to be close to memory.”
Hock spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier at the AI Data Pipeline Forum, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed agentic workflows and the importance of inference speed. (* Disclosure below.)
Why agentic workflows make speed a requirement
Cerebras’ Wafer-Scale Engine is more than 50 times as large as previous conventional processors, and the company claims its inference performance is 10 to 15 times faster than that of competing GPU-based platforms. In agentic workflows, that means more agents working together, Hock explained.
“One question from you or from me into an agentic system doesn’t just spawn one intelligent agent going down and doing some work or answering a question for us, but it spawns a family of daughter agents that are all doing different work and all coordinating together,” Hock said. “That’s where speed really makes the difference.”
Cerebras reported its first-quarter 2026 results in June. Over the past two months, foundation labs and enterprises have moved away from tokenmaxxing and toward getting the most value out of each token, Hock noted.
“They’re making decisions based on that value maximization paradigm on models, on datasets and on infrastructure,” he said. “On the infrastructure side, to bring it home to Cerebras, what we’re seeing is that our end users are actually finding the greatest value out of the fastest tokens.”

articles.title: A Chinese rival to DGX Spark and Ryzen AI Halo emerges in Sipeed’s AX8860-based MaixStation
articles.text:
Sipeed reveals Chinese-made DGX Spark and Ryzen AI Halo rival, expected to cost $3,999 — MaixStation pairs Axera’s AX8860P with 128GB of LPDDR5X at 273 GB/s, with promising local AI performance claims
Its NPU toolchain is due at month’s end, with units shipping after a year-end Kickstarter.
A Chinese rival to the DGX Spark and the Ryzen AI Halo, at least on paper, has emerged with Sipeed’s announcement of the MaixStation. The system, built on Axera’s new AX8860P, is in the same memory class with 128GB of LPDDR5X on a 256-bit bus at 273 GB/s. Sipeed told Tom’s Hardware Premium it expects the 128GB model to cost around $3,999, with launch discounts on Kickstarter, putting it level with the 128GB Ryzen AI Halo and well under the DGX Spark’s current MSRP of $6,950. Sign-ups are open now on Sipeed’s MaixStation page ahead of a Kickstarter campaign at the end of the year, with units shipping within three months after it closes. The NPU toolchain is due by the end of this month.
The AX8860P is a 16-core Arm Cortex-A55 part with an in-house NPU rated at 256 TOPS at native FP4 with no sparsity. The chip is produced in the 6nm process, Axera says. Sipeed claims the system has 25% faster prefill and 30% faster decode than the DGX Spark when running Qwen 27B (the company did not disclose which specific model, but later details that it expects a single MaixStation to run Qwen 3.8-27B) from a single node.
In its email, though, the company put its MaixStation about 10% ahead on both prefill and decode when compared to DGX Spark, with FP4 on each machine, with speculative decoding off, and said newer runs with a wider lead aren’t official yet. It teased the new product on its X account, showing a photo from the AX8860P’s announcement at an industrial fair in Shanghai on Tuesday.
| Sipeed MaixStation vs Nvidia DGX Spark vs AMD Ryzen AI Halo |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Header Cell - Column 0 | Sipeed MaixStation (Axera AX8860P) | Nvidia DGX Spark (GB10) | AMD Ryzen AI Halo (Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495) | AMD Ryzen AI Halo (Ryzen AI Max+ 395) | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Status | Kickstarter at the end of 2026; specs are Sipeed’s claims | 128GB on sale; 64GB due Oct. 23 through partners | On sale | On sale | 
| CPU | 16 Arm Cortex-A55 cores | 20 Arm cores (10 Cortex-X925, 10 Cortex-A725) | 16 Zen 5 cores | 16 Zen 5 cores | 
| Memory | 128GB LPDDR5X; 512GB on MaixStation Pro | 128GB LPDDR5X; 64GB through partners | 192GB LPDDR5X-8533 | 128GB LPDDR5X-8000 | 
| Memory bandwidth | 273 GB/s | 273 GB/s | 273 GB/s | 256 GB/s | 
| AI compute (rated peak) | NPU: 256 TOPS FP4, no sparsity | Blackwell GPU: up to 1 PFLOP FP4 with sparsity, about 500 TFLOPS dense | Radeon 8065S GPU (40 CUs): up to 61 TFLOPS FP16; NPU: up to 55 TOPS | Radeon 8060S GPU (40 CUs); NPU: up to 50 TOPS | 
| Software | Debian 13; NPU toolchain due at the end of October; Sipeed claims vLLM, SGLang and PyTorch support | DGX OS (Ubuntu 24.04 LTS) with CUDA and Nvidia’s AI software stack preinstalled | ROCm, validated as a “Best-Known Configuration”; Linux now, Windows “coming soon” | Linux or Windows 11 Pro | 
| Networking | 10G SFP+; 256 Gbps C2C link (up to 384 Gbps), up to eight nodes without a switch, per Sipeed | 10GbE; ConnectX-7 at 200 Gbps, up to four systems (four need a switch) | 10GbE | 10GbE | 
| Price | About $3,999 expected (128GB), per Sipeed | $6,950 (128GB); 64GB from $4,999 through partners from Oct. 23 | $7,299.99 (Linux) | $3,999.99 | 
For comparison, the DGX Spark also comes in 128GB at 273 GB/s with another SKU at 64GB, the two models priced at $6,950 and from $4,999. The former has been on sale since October 2025, at its current price since Oct. 2, and the latter is expected through partners on Oct. 23. For AMD, its Ryzen AI Halo has a 192GB Max+ PRO 495 model at 273 GB/s, released earlier this week at $7,299.99 for the Linux version, and the 128GB Max+ 395 model with 256 GB/s at $3,999.99. In all cases, 256-bit LPDDR5X is used, so the salient differences are memory capacity, compute, and software.
Memory is also a big share of what these systems cost: the best U.S. price for a 128GB DDR5 kit was $3,399 in August, and TrendForce expects conventional DRAM contract prices to rise another 10–15% this quarter. As for its unit prices, Sipeed says it used current DRAM prices rather than stock bought last year. It also suggested buyers could supply their own SSD, which could cut the price further, clarifying that the MaixStation takes a standard M.2 2280 drive rather than the Spark’s less common 2242.
Software-wise, the Spark ships with DGX OS, which is Nvidia’s build of Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, with CUDA and Nvidia’s AI software stack preinstalled. AMD validates ROCm, drivers, models, and frameworks together as a “Best-Known Configuration.” Neither the Spark nor the PRO 495 ships with Windows yet, though AMD says Windows versions are “coming soon,” and the Max+ 395 model already offers Windows 11 Pro. Sipeed, aside from its upcoming NPU toolchain, claims support for vLLM, SGLang, and PyTorch, with Axera adding ONNX, Hugging Face (HF) model formats, and an OpenAI-compatible API. MaixStation itself ships with Debian 13 and Linux 6.18, and Windows support for the PCIe card will depend on demand, Sipeed says.
Chinese solutions already exist on AMD silicon, such as GMKtec’s 192GB Evo-X5 Pro at $6,799 to $7,099. There’s also Minisforum’s MS-S1 Max-P495. What’s new with the MaixStation is the Chinese silicon underneath.
The Axera AX8860P, as recently launched, has, in addition to the above specs, PCIe 5.0 support, 64-channel video decode with 16-channel encode, and support for multiple form factors, including a single-slot, four-chip PCIe card capable of running up to 512GB of memory, with mini and pocket PC products planned. Like the eight-core AX8850 in Radxa’s and M5Stack’s M.2 accelerator cards, it pairs Arm Cortex-A55 cores with Axera’s NPU, now with twice the cores and up to 128GB of memory instead of 8GB. Two- and four-chip cascades reach a theoretical 512 and 1,024 TOPS, respectively, at a claimed scaling efficiency of about 80%. The CPU, against the Spark’s Cortex-X925 and Halo’s Zen 5, is small and in-order. It’s sufficient for the NPU but potentially more limited for other tasks.
The box itself measures about 11 × 11 × 3 cm and draws about 40W in typical use, powered over USB-C, according to Sipeed. Its ports include 10G SFP+, USB-C, an M.2 2280 slot for a PCIe 5.0 SSD, and an MCIO 8i connector for linking a second unit.
Sipeed says the MaixStation supports all configurations, that’s single, dual, and quad node, plus any “PCIe card mode for any card count you want.” The interconnect in use is a 256 Gbps C2C connection (up to 384 Gbps) “without [an] extra switch needed, and [up to] 8-node.”
The contrast is with the Spark’s QSFP ports, and Nvidia’s datasheet says linking four Sparks “requires [an] external switch.” The math, at 32 Gbps per lane, works out to 256 Gbps with the default eight lanes and 384 Gbps with the maximum of twelve. Remote-access test units and a few review units will follow during the Kickstarter campaign, the company told us.
Sipeed also commented on the openness of the platform, saying, “Yes, bsp sdk is open, you can use AI to port any distribution on it!” Sipeed has previously sold Axera boards, with products dating back to 2022 using the AX620A, AX650N, and AX630C.
The claims of the MaixStation being faster in some workloads are coupled with Sipeed saying “In fact you need [to] ask why DGX is so slow…” with potential financial implications, as Nvidia “just [wants to make] more money from users.” When an X user argued that Sipeed must be using extreme quantization at that bandwidth, the company suggested that the Spark’s specs may be overstated.
By our math, the decode claim is plausible with a 4-bit 27B model, which sits at about 13.5GB. Performance on comparable machines tops out near 20 tokens per second, which means around 270 GB/s. Prefill, which is compute-bound, is a harder sell, but Sipeed stated that “DGX Spark 1000TOPS is fake ‘sparse.’” That 1 PFLOP figure does rely on sparsity, but the DGX Spark’s dense rate of about 500 TFLOPS is still around double the AX8860P’s 256 TOPS.
Axera’s current stack has Pulsar2 as the NPU compiler and toolchain, with version 8.0 on HuggingFace last week, and the V7.0 docs already list the chip as the AX8860. There’s no operator support list for the chip yet, and the docs’ LLM chapter for older chips lists weights down to 4-bit integers but no FP4. Neither the ax-llm runtime nor AXCL, the host-side PCIe driver and runtime for Axera’s cards, lists the chip yet. Sipeed says the end-of-month release is AXDSL, a kernel-programming language, plus the Pulsar2 source code, and that SGLang and vLLM run on a custom backend built on it, so Hugging Face models run without a conversion step.
Enthusiasts are already eager to know the final specifications and pricing for the different models. On paper, as far as local LLM machines go, the MaixStation matches the Spark on memory size and claimed bandwidth, and the Max+ PRO 495 Halo on bandwidth alone. Testing performance claims will also have to wait for the toolchain and sample machines land, hopefully before the end of the year.
Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.

articles.title: ASUS Republic of Gamers Announces Availability of ROG XBOX Ally X20
articles.text:
Thursday, October 15th 2026
ASUS Republic of Gamers Announces Availability of ROG XBOX Ally X20
ASUS Republic of Gamers (ROG) is proud to announce that the ROG XBOX Ally X20 is today available for purchase. A handheld that's both a throwback to gaming two decades ago and a vision of what's next, it's housed in a translucent black chassis with a vibrant gold internal structure. The XBOX Ally X20 features ROG's all-new Nebula HDR Display featuring a 7.4-inch OLED panel, as well as the AMD Ryzen AI Z2 Extreme processor for ample gaming horsepower. With a host of software updates that enhance the user experience, the ROG XBOX Ally X20 is ready to play anywhere. It's available as a standalone device for US$1,299 or bundled with the ROG XREAL R1 Edition 20 Gaming AR Glasses, a custom dbrand Killswitch case and a Pelican Protector Case for US$2,499.
Available to buy today
Starting today, the ROG XBOX Ally X20 is available for purchase, both as a standalone device or as part of an ultra-premium bundle. The US$1299 XBOX Ally X20 joins the existing ROG XBOX Ally lineup of gaming handhelds. Both the ROG XBOX Ally and ROG XBOX Ally X are also still available for sale at their original MSRPs of US$599 and US$999 respectively. Together, these three devices provide a range of options for players.The XBOX Ally X20 is an evolution and a celebration of everything that made the original ROG XBOX Ally special. Featuring translucent black plastic for the chassis, it harkens back to a distinct era of gaming that veterans will remember fondly. This translucence also offers a peek under the hood to the revamped high-performance cooling system and incredible handheld silicon from AMD, with just a hint of the gold-accented internal structure. Crafted exclusively for the 20th anniversary of the formation of the Republic of Gamers in 2006, this special edition XBOX Ally X20 is sure to look incredible in any collection. Gamers can pick their perfect loadout and celebrate 20 years of ROG.
Equipped with magnetic TMR sensors in the joysticks designed to significantly reduce the potential for stick drift and have a tight 3% dead zone, the XBOX Ally X20 gives gamers millimeter precision without four-axis snapping thanks to a new algorithm. A huge boon for fighting game pros, the XBOX Ally X20 features a transforming D-pad that can seamlessly switch from four-way to eight-way movement, with no tools required. The face buttons have been engineered to sit flush with the chassis when fully pressed, and when paired with a lighter actuation force, they deliver seamless inputs. New rubberized grips increase control and comfort over long sessions, and impulse triggers deliver immersive haptic feedback to make every action feel precise.
The ROG XBOX Ally X20 Bundle also includes a pair of ROG XREAL R1 Edition 20 Gaming AR Glasses. Whether at home or on-the-go, the ROG XREAL R1 Edition 20 Gaming AR Glasses step up gaming immersion with a 171-inch virtual screen at 4 meters. The 57° field of view covers 95% of the focused viewing area, and the Micro-OLED display delivers a 240 Hz refresh rate with a near-instantaneous 0.01 ms response time. Native 3DoF tracking allows the screen to follow head movements, and Anchor Mode keeps it in one place during play. Paired with a custom dbrand Killswitch for ROG XBOX Ally X20 with an exclusive skin and stick caps, and a custom Pelican Protector case that has room for every accessory in the bundle, this is a true collector's item.
Incredible performance
The ROG XBOX Ally X20 also features under-the-hood improvements. Its cooling system has been redesigned to focus the airflow down three main paths: behind the OLED panel, heatsink fins, and directly to the processor. This three-pronged approach keeps component temperatures low while also maintaining a comfortable skin temperature for the handgrips, critical for comfort during extended gaming sessions. The fans themselves have also been redesigned, with fewer blades but a larger diameter, which improves overall airflow by 20%, with an 11% increase heatsink fin surface area.
The XBOX Ally X20 also supports variable refresh rate (VRR) technology, which dynamically adapts the display's refresh rate to game's frame rate to help reduce screen tearing and provide a smoother experience when there are any unexpected framerate drops in game to eliminate screen tearing.
Revamped software experience
The launch of the ROG XBOX Ally X20 also marks a new chapter for Armoury Crate Special Edition, the custom software that powers the ROG Ally family. A suite of new features improves every aspect of the user experience, letting users spend more time gaming.
The UI scaling has been refined, allowing for easier readability across menus and game libraries. Aura Sync functionality has also been upgraded for the XBOX Ally X20, and now features two new modes, Reactive and Immersion. Reactive Mode lights up in the direction the joystick is pushed, while Immersion Mode lights up in the direction of in-game sounds.
With its brand-new OLED ROG Nebula Display, the XBOX Ally X20 also offers two modes to let gamers optimize their HDR experience. HDR Native faithfully reproduces the creator's original colors, lighting, and shadow details with punchy HDR highlights, while HDR Vivid boosts the colors and intensity for an extra vibrant image.
Customizing gaming playstyles is now easier than ever with Default Game Profile 2.0. Anytime a gamer manually tweaks their performance settings, they can instantly save their optimal configuration—like wattage and power limits—directly to a specific game's profile with just a single click. The major hot keys on all ROG Ally devices, including the Command Center, Library, and Action buttons, are all now customizable. From a simple menu is ACSE, gamers can easily map these buttons to other functions to make the device fit their exact playstyle.
In addition, an all-new Travel Mode automatically limits charging power to 65 W, offering better compatibility when charging on planes or trains built-in seat power outlets. This feature turns on automatically when Airplane Mode is enabled, or users can flip it on manually.
Finally, Armoury Crate SE is also changing how it handles large updates. Cutting-edge features can now be accessed on an opt-in basis on a preview channel for power users, which will allow valuable feedback to be provided before being launched as automatic updates to the wider userbase.
