articles.title: EU negotiates sanction swap with China to rescue critical ASML supplier — German coatings firm faces shutdown without Chinese rare earths
articles.text:
EU negotiates sanction swap with China to rescue critical ASML supplier — German coatings firm faces shutdown without Chinese rare earths
Sindlhauser risks going out of business in the coming months if the sanctions remain
The EU is currently in talks with China to lift restrictions the country imposed on Sindlhauser Materials GmbH, a German company in ASML’s supply chain, as the sanctions risk putting the company out of business. In return, the EU would remove restrictions it placed on one unnamed Chinese firm accused of aiding Russia in the war with Ukraine, according to an Oct. 14 Bloomberg report citing people familiar with the matter.
The deal was discussed during EU Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security Maroš Šefčovič’s visit to Beijing. The EU is expected to make the first move, with any delisting on its end requiring unanimous support from member states. Both sides also agreed to share more information and give advance warning on future export restrictions.
In July 2026, China put Sindlhauser, a German precision-manufacturing and advanced-coatings firm, on its export-control list, along with 13 other European companies, in apparent retaliation for the EU’s 21st Russia sanctions package, which sanctioned several Chinese firms accused of supplying Moscow with components that can be used to make weapons. Beijing’s official reason was the firms’ alleged dealings with Taiwan.
China’s selection of Sindlhauser is not random, as the company sits in ASML’s supply chain. According to Bloomberg, officials believe Beijing has spent the last year and a half gathering information on Western supply chains, and used the data to identify the seemingly obscure German firm as a pressure point on the world’s most important chipmaking-equipment company.
Sindlhauser relies almost entirely on Chinese rare earths and critical minerals. Therefore, the restrictions, which ban Chinese exporters from selling dual-use items to the firm, cut off its main source of input. They also prohibit foreign companies and individuals from passing on China-origin dual-use items to the firm, thus preventing Sindlhauser from simply sourcing the same materials through a third-party distributor.
After the listing, which initially sparked panic over the company’s survival, the German government and Bavaria’s state government stepped in, helping the company explore workarounds such as alternative suppliers and recycling existing materials. However, due to its heavy dependence on China, Sindlhauser now faces the risk of going out of business in the coming months if the sanctions remain.
EU officials in Brussels had been raising the case with Beijing for weeks, culminating in the delisting swap discussed during Šefčovič’s visit. The incident highlights China’s influence on several aspects of the global technology supply chain, including semiconductor manufacturing, which is critical to the AI boom. The country placed export restrictions on several rare earth metals, limiting their availability across the supply chain. Meanwhile, the West has been investing heavily in domestic supply chains to reduce reliance on China.

articles.title: Targeted ads delivered 0-click exploits to install mercenary malware
articles.text:
Researchers say that mercenary hackers laced ads with zero-click exploits that installed sophisticated malware on the devices of targeted individuals when they did nothing other than load a website or open an installed app.
The finding, published Thursday by the University of Toronto’s Citizen Lab, said the incident is likely to be the first confirmation of zero-click mercenary spyware delivered through targeted ads. The attacks, which worked on iOS and Android devices, are particularly pernicious because they work without requiring any interaction from the target and are invisible unless users run special forensic hardware or software. Citizen Lab said it confirmed that AdFection, as it named the campaign, infected 45 devices at international media organization Al Jazeera in 2024 and 2025.
A clear warning signal
“This investigation should … serve as a clear warning signal to news organizations around the world that they may be being actively targeted via this new threat,” Citizen Lab researchers wrote. “This targeting may happen both in newsrooms and to individual journalists, editors, and other staff members.” Their report went on to say: “The distribution of spyware via targeted ads represents a security risk not only for potential victims but also for states and civil society at large.”
The ads were provided by Discover-Tech, an Israeli company that brands itself as a legitimate advertising company, but Citizen Lab said it operates as a facilitator for multiple mercenary spyware partners. The company acts as a broker between parties that want to display their ads and publishers or app makers that seek revenue in return for showing them. In this capacity, Discover-Tech acts as a “bridge between ad vendors and the mercenary spyware ecosystem,” a role that appears to be “Discover-Tech’s primary purpose,” Citizen Lab said.
The brokering involves a bidding process in which advertisers offer a fee in exchange for their ads appearing on the devices of individuals in particular demographics. Using users’ unique mobile ID, location, IP address, and other breadcrumbs, the brokers are able to assemble detailed profiles of millions of people. Citizen Lab said it obtained more than 4 billion bidding records handled by Discover-Tech. They revealed that Discover-Tech ads were displayed in over 70,000 mobile apps and more than 120,000 websites between March and June 2026.
You can leave your ad blocker on as a sub, or turn it off, and it just won't make any real difference. Nor will we care.
For anyone who's not a subscriber, and running an ad blocker for any reason, please do consider subscribing. It's like $2 a month, you support us, you get a better reading experience and a bunch of perks, and we're constantly trying to find more ways to add value to it.
All we can do is ask for your support, we're not forcing anyone. But it does make a difference.

articles.title: Hackers hijacked 1,900 GitHub accounts. Then they went after 30,000 repos.
articles.text:
Hackers hijacked 1,900 GitHub accounts. Then they went after 30,000 repos.
Hackers accessed roughly 1,900 GitHub accounts, then used them to slip credential-stealing workflows into more than 30,000 repositories. The malicious GitHub Actions jobs targeted CI/CD secrets, cloud access keys, and AI provider API keys. GitGuardian tracked the GhostAction campaign as it intensified, with the biggest push on October 8 and 9, when the attackers reached repositories belonging to about 3,000 users and organizations and tried to extract 3,174 secrets.
How the accounts were compromised
The tj-actions/changed-files compromise poisoned a shared Action used by thousands of repositories. GhostAction took a different route, using stolen developer credentials to modify workflows directly, with no vulnerability in GitHub Actions itself.
It’s unclear how the attackers obtained those credentials, but StepSecurity’s October 9 analysis points to personal access tokens pulled from credential dumps as the likely source, though the initial compromise hasn’t been confirmed.
With access to the repositories, the attackers could then add disguised workflows of standard security jobs, while using names like security-audit.yml or github_actions_security.yml. Since the files referenced secrets already used by legitimate builds, it gave the malicious jobs the chance to collect those credentials when they ran and send them to an attacker-controlled server.
Scanning the full Git history
The October variant went beyond the secrets explicitly referenced by workflows, using actions/checkout@v4 with fetch-depth: 0 to scan the working tree and Git history for AWS keys, GitHub and GitLab PATs, Google and Firebase keys, and API tokens from Anthropic, OpenAI and OpenRouter. Later versions captured surrounding lines to pair AWS key IDs with their corresponding secret access keys.
The harvested credentials were sent over HTTP to 193.32.204.199, including keys removed from the current codebase but still present in Git history.
GitHub blocked the malicious workflows
“This payload was deployed in multiple phases,” GitGuardian wrote, describing an initial push to about 160 previously targeted victims and, 20 minutes later, a far larger deployment into 28,000 new repositories across October 8 and 9.
“This payload was deployed in multiple phases.”
The total number of stolen credentials remains unknown. GitGuardian counted 3,174 secrets targeted for extraction and confirmed some exfiltration during the October campaign, but it didn’t determine how many distinct credentials reached the attackers.
During the August and September campaign, GitGuardian identified malicious workflows in 772 public repositories across 373 users and organizations. Of the 3,669 workflow runs recorded across 605 repositories, only 499 executed, with 336 completing successfully and exfiltrating 26 secrets from 13 repositories.
GitHub’s approval controls stopped most of the bad workflows, but attackers simply recycled 92 older ones left behind from earlier attacks, including infrastructure active since September 2025. To make matters worse, GitGuardian found that by October 5, only 16% of the affected repositories — 124 out of 772 — had been cleaned up.
To make matters worse, GitGuardian found that by October 5, only 16% of the affected repositories — 124 out of 772 — had been cleaned up.
Rotate exposed secrets and tokens
GitHub audit records and PAT activity can help identify which accounts modified .github/workflows/, while Actions run histories show which jobs executed and what secrets they could access. Any compromised account still holding write access needs to have its credentials revoked, even if the malicious workflow has already been removed.
Cloud keys, deployment credentials, registry tokens, and AI provider API keys potentially exposed during the attack also need to be revoked or rotated, including those deleted from the codebase months ago but still valid when the attackers scanned Git history.
Any compromised account still holding write access needs to have its credentials revoked, even if the malicious workflow has already been removed.

articles.title: Windows has fixed an issue with 'Always on VPN' in its latest update — but it seems to have brought more issues with it
articles.text:
Windows has fixed an issue with 'Always on VPN' in its latest update — but it seems to have brought more issues with it
One step forward…
Microsoft has released a minor Windows update to address connection issues with Always On VPN, with users reporting other fixes as a seemingly unintended consequence.
As Bleeping Computer reports, users reported connection issues with Microsoft’s Always On VPN standard following a Windows update in September 2026. The tech titan has released the KB 5127646 and KB5127648 cumulative updates in order to address the problem.
Always On VPN is a connection standard built into Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server that lets VPNs activate as soon as a user’s computer detects an active internet connection. It’s the underlying technology that allows some of the best VPNs to offer automatic connections on Windows computers.
In an alert shared with IT administrators in September 2026 (via Bleeping Computer), Microsoft acknowledged a bug that caused Always On VPN to fail if the computer couldn’t establish an initial internet connection.
The alert noted that repeated connection attempts could display an error reading “The specified port is already in use”, suggesting that Windows hadn’t been able to recognise a failed connection. The issue affected computers and servers running Windows 11 24H2 or newer.
Naturally, this was a problem for users and organisations who leave their VPN to activate automatically by default. And, though such failures could generate error messages, it’s possible that this bug could’ve left users unprotected against malicious tracking or data harvesting, a particular concern for large organisations.
Microsoft has also given details of a temporary fix for users and organisations that are unable to install the cumulative updates that correct this issue: “IT administrators can mitigate this issue by changing the Always On VPN profile from automatic protocol selection to a single protocol, either SSTP only or IKEv2 only, depending on their environment and configuration.”
Redditor reports a bonus fix – but others report new issues
According to user reports, it seems that Microsoft’s Always On VPN patch has improved other VPN connections, though it's unclear whether this was intentional or an unintended bonus.
Reddit user Canada_Ottawa shared that their Surfshark connection had improved in both speed and stability overnight after installing the MS Tuesday, 2026 10 13 Windows 11 update.
The user said that their VPN connection had been unstable for “about two months” prior to this patch, especially when waking their computer from Sleep mode.
On the flip side, other online users have shared their frustration at new issues arising with the most recent Windows patch.
User ephycalyptus said that they could no longer connect to their company WiFi after the update, noting that the network uses Aruba access points. Commenters have suggested the update has affected 802.1x PEAP connections and NTLMv1 authentication protocols.
A forum post on Microsoft Learn suggests similar issues. User Supply-PWC writes: “After installing KB5127648, Windows 11 clients can no longer authenticate to our WPA2-Enterprise (802.1X/PEAP) wireless network. Authentication starts but never completes [...] The issue reproduces across multiple hardware vendors and wireless chipsets.”
Overall, it seems that Microsoft has fixed one problem only to set off another. We’ll be on the lookout for updates from the firm itself in the coming days.
Jamie is freelance journalist who has written for TechRadar and MusicRadar as well as various specialist news outlets and music blogs. A lifelong tech-obsessive, Jamie began his writing career as a music blogger before studying journalism at Goldsmiths College, and worked at TechRadar between 2024 and 2026. He thinks the iPhone 5S is the greatest phone of all time, but is currently an Android user.

articles.title: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security warns of AI scams ahead of holiday shopping season
articles.text:
The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security published guidance for safe online shopping ahead of the holiday buying season. The centre warned of increasing risk from AI, which is helping enable more robust scams.
According to the guidance, “threat actors use increasingly convincing techniques to steal personal and financial information, redirect payments and compromise online accounts.” These techniques put personal and business information and assets at risk.
With that in mind, the guidance outlines common threats and how AI is aiding those threats, how to recognize scams and protect yourself, and finally, what to do if you fall for a scam.
Common threats
The cyber centre outlined some common ways that threat actors can steal information, such as creating fake storefronts, payment processing sites, and/or fake checkout pages to steal information. The centre also warned about insecure websites (e.g. those that use HTTP instead of HTTPS), and online stores that don’t offer basic consumer protections.
Other things to watch out for include impersonation scams where threat actors pretend to be other companies or retailers, fraudulent links or QR codes, and requests to move payments outside of secure channels, such as using e-transfer, gift cards, or cryptocurrency.
AI makes many of the above behaviours much, much easier for scammers. It can help create convincing, professional-looking websites, ads, reviews, and more.
Elsewhere, the guidance warns of AI-powered shopping assistants that can make recommendations or even complete purchases.
“AI tools cannot reliably determine whether a seller, website or offer is trustworthy or fraudulent in the same way a person can. You should remain actively involved in shopping decisions and verify sellers and payment details. Treat AI-generated recommendations as guidance, not assurances of legitimacy,” the guidance says.
This warning is particularly prevalent amid the rise of AI apps like Meta’s Muse, which claims to be able to handle various tasks like shopping on behalf of users. However, not only are there risks with using AI shopping assistants, but these apps often have their own security problems. Muse, for example, had a serious security flaw at launch that allowed any app or terminal command to essentially take over the AI assistant and do whatever attackers wanted on the victim’s device. Yikes!
I’d go one step further than the cyber centre guidance and encourage people not to use AI apps and tools like this at all, given the significant security risks involved.
How to recognize scams and protect yourself
When shopping online, there are a few things to watch for that can help you spot potential scams.
Look for things like poor design that makes sites look unprofessional, or for elements like buttons or links that don’t work properly. Legitimate sites typically also offer policies for users, such as privacy or refunds and returns — check for those and make sure the policies in place make sense. Similarly, look for clear, accurate contact information. Finally — and this advice is universally helpful — you should question any requests for personal or financial information, especially if it’s not needed for or relevant to your purchase.
However, scams go beyond websites, so the Centre for Cyber Security also shared tips for recognizing other types of scams, like suspicious messages or offers. Be wary of offers that seem too good to be true and of pressure tactics that urge shoppers to act quickly. Moreover, watch for unexpected or higher-than-usual charges, and be wary of unexpected follow-up messages. (For example, there’s an ongoing carrier scam that tricks people into sending recently purchased products to scammers.)
Along with recognizing signs of possible scams, there are actions Canadians should take to protect themselves when shopping online, even with legitimate retailers.
When shopping, always do your research — look up independent reviews from beyond the retailer’s website, look into how long a retailer has been operating, and search for complaints and reports of scams or other customer issues.
For online browsing in general, make sure you’re connecting to secure websites. Look for HTTPS in the URL, which signifies a secure connection (most web browsers will show an icon like a shield or padlock in the URL bar to indicate whether a site is secure, and may even show warnings if you connect to an insecure website). Always double-check the URL, since common scams rely on tricking people with fake URLs. For example, a fraudulent site pretending to be Amazon might replace the ‘o’ with a zero so that it looks legit at a glance. This is extra important on mobile, where URLs are often shortened because of the limited screen space. And never click links that are sent to you via email or text message.
Finally, it’s important to protect your accounts by creating strong passwords or passphrases and using multi-factor authentication (MFA) whenever possible. While the cyber centre guidance doesn’t mention this, it’s a great idea to use a password manager, which can help users create and store strong, unique passwords for every account they use.
What to do if you fall for a scam
Wrapping things up, if you do fall for fraud, there are a few things you should do after.
First, notify relevant people, like your friends and family or your employer so they can help.
Next, contact your financial institution or credit card company to report the fraud. They’ll be able to help you take steps to secure your finances or possibly reverse fraudulent charges.
Third, reset your affected accounts, such as email or social media, as well as any accounts that used a similar password to the one that was compromised. (Again, if you’re using one password, or a variation of one password, across multiple online accounts — don’t! If you do that, one compromised account can expose everything.)
Finally, report the incident to Canada’s Anti-Fraud Centre. You should do this even if you didn’t lose any money, because knowing about ongoing scams can help spread awareness and aid in stopping fraud.
For more details on how to protect yourself during the holiday shopping season, check out the full guidance.

articles.title: Apple wants Chrome users to switch to Safari, claims up to five extra hours of video playback on a Mac
articles.text:
The takeaway: Apple is making a fresh pitch to Chrome users: switch to Safari and spend less time plugged in. Its newly launched "Stay on Safari" campaign promises up to five additional hours of video streaming on a Mac, faster page loads, and stronger default privacy protections. The question is whether these gains in efficiency and privacy are enough to lure users away from the tools and features that keep them loyal to Chrome.
StatCounter figures put Chrome's browser market share at 66.36%, compared with Safari's 18.27%. Apple's campaign aims to narrow that gap by making browser efficiency a more prominent consideration.
The campaign challenges Chrome's dominance with an argument rooted in Apple's control over its hardware and software. Apple develops Safari's WebKit engine for its devices, allowing it to optimize the browser for its own chips. That gives the company a direct way to improve power efficiency and performance, although its advertised results apply to specific tasks rather than every type of browsing.
Apple claims Safari loads frequently visited websites up to 35% faster than Chrome on macOS. Its test used snapshot versions of 12 popular websites under simulated network conditions. The computers were 15-inch MacBook Air laptops equipped with M5 chips and 16GB of unified memory.
Those details limit what the figure tells us about everyday use. The comparison does not establish a 35% improvement across all websites, Macs, or internet connections. Instead, it measures performance across a selected group of sites on a specific hardware configuration.
The battery-life claim requires a similar caveat. Apple advertises up to five additional hours of video streaming on a single charge, not five extra hours for every browser task. Streaming video and loading web pages are different workloads, and the campaign makes separate claims for each.
Safari's close integration with Apple's hardware is central to its pitch. Its developers can optimize WebKit for Apple silicon. Chrome, which is built on Chromium, uses a multi-process architecture that has drawn criticism for its memory consumption.
That architectural difference helps explain the technical debate, but it does not, by itself, prove Apple's advertised gains. The campaign's figures remain Apple's own measurements, and their relevance depends on how closely a user's activity matches the tested workloads.
Safari's privacy pitch focuses on its default settings. The browser automatically blocks third-party cookies and includes Intelligent Tracking Prevention. Apple presents these built-in protections as an advantage over Chrome, without requiring users to adjust their settings.
Google has also faced criticism over Chrome's AI features, including the browser's automatic download of a 4GB Gemini Nano model. That issue adds to the scrutiny surrounding Chrome, but it is separate from the tests underpinning Apple's speed and battery-life claims.
Safari also includes Reader Mode, Profiles, and native Apple Pay support, along with integration across Apple devices. These features give users additional reasons to consider switching.
Chrome has its own practical advantages. Its extensive extension ecosystem and synchronization across Windows and Android help users work across different operating systems. Someone who relies on a particular Chrome extension or regularly switches between a Mac and a Windows computer may have less reason to switch, even if Safari consumes less power.
Apple's strongest claims are specific enough to test: longer video playback and faster loading of frequently visited websites. For Mac users, the question is whether those gains hold up in their own browsing and whether they outweigh the extensions and cross-platform features they would leave behind.

articles.title: Cuánto cuesta la criptomoneda Bitcoin este jueves
articles.text:
El bitcoin fue la primera criptomoneda que salió al mercado. Ideada por Satoshi Nakamoto en 2008, esta divisa digital promovía un ideal libertario y buscaba poner en jaque a las instituciones monetarias y financieras tradicionales luego de la crisis financiera mundial que se vivió ese año.
La victoria electoral de Donald Trump significó un movimiento positivo para las principales criptomonedas del mercado. A finales de 2024, bitcoin registró un nuevo máximo histórico que logró superar los 107.000 dólares por unidad, después de que el presidente estadounidense reiteró su idea de crear una reserva estratégica de la criptodivisa en Estados Unidos.
Las divisas digitales serán un foco de atención durante este año, las iniciativas del presidente de Estados Unidos y el desarrollo de nuevos modelos de inteligencia artificial fungirán un papel importante en la cotización de estos activos. Después del lanzamiento del nuevo modelo de IA chino DeepSeek, BTC y otras criptos cayeron en la mayoría de los mercados de valores.
Costo de la criptomoneda Bitcoin
El precio de la criptomoneda bitcoin para este día a las 14:00 horas (UTC) es de 80206.39 dólares. Esto quiere decir que el activo digital registró un cambio de -3.17% en el último día, así como un movimiento de 0.0% en la última hora.
Por su nivel de capitalización, esta moneda digital ocupa la posición #1 entre las más populares.
Bitcoin alcanza un nuevo récord y lidera el auge en el mercado de las criptomonedas
En marzo del año pasado el bitcoin ha logrado un nuevo máximo histórico, superando los valores anteriores y reafirmándose como la criptomoneda más importante en el mercado, acercándose a los 73 mil dólares. Este récord se obtuvo en medio de un flujo sin precedentes de inversiones hacia las criptomonedas, un acontecimiento notable para el sector financiero digital.
El aumento en el valor de bitcoin ocurre en un contexto donde hay un entrante masivo de capital hacia las criptomonedas, lo que indica un creciente interés y confianza de los inversores en estos activos. La subida del precio beneficia no solo a bitcoin sino que también tiene un impacto positivo en el mercado de las criptomonedas en general, favoreciendo una mayor estabilidad y visibilidad, de acuerdo a un análisis de Bloomberg.
Expertos financiaron este aumento a diferentes factores, como la adopción institucional de las criptomonedas, la búsqueda de alternativas de inversión debido a la incertidumbre económica mundial y la innovación continua en la tecnología blockchain que respalda a bitcoin y otras divisas digitales. Esta combinación de factores ha creado un entorno propicio para el crecimiento continuo en el valor de Bitcoin.
Cómo adquirir criptomonedas
Para comprarlas e intercambiarlas se utilizan portales especializados. Su valor varía en función de la oferta, de la demanda y del compromiso de los usuarios, por lo que puede cambiar más rápido que el dinero tradicional, pero mientras más gente esté interesada y quiera comprar determinada divisa, mayor será su valor.
No obstante, quien invierte en este tipo de monedas digitales debe tener muy claro que esta forma trae consigo un elevado riesgo al capital, pues, así como puede haber un incremento, también puede tener inesperadamente un desplome y acabar con los ahorros de sus usuarios.
Para almacenarlas, los usuarios deben contar con un monedero digital o wallet, que en realidad es un software a través del cual es posible guardar, enviar y hacer transacciones de las criptomonedas. En realidad, este tipo de monederos sólo guarda las claves que marcan la propiedad y el derecho de una persona sobre cierta criptomoneda, por lo que estos códigos son los que en realidad se deben proteger.

articles.title: ServiceNow adds AI agent controls and employee automation tools - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
ServiceNow adds AI agent controls and employee automation tools
ServiceNow Inc. today announced new controls for governing artificial intelligence agents alongside updates to its EmployeeWorks information portal (pictured) that let employees build specialized assistants and automate routine tasks without writing code.
The announcements address two connected challenges for businesses expanding their use of autonomous AI: giving workers tools that can act across enterprise systems and ensuring those tools stay within approved boundaries.
The centerpiece of the governance announcement is AI Passport, a cryptographically signed credential that defines an agent’s identity, permitted actions, accessible systems and accountable owner. Issued through ServiceNow’s AI Control Tower governance platform, it is designed to carry those permissions across agents, tools and vendors, with checks performed as work executes.
“Without that baseline, every guardrail is just advisory,” said Nenshad Bardoliwalla, senior vice president of AI products at ServiceNow.
The company says identifying agents and monitoring their behavior aren’t enough without enforceable limits on their authority. AI Passport draws on business context from ServiceNow’s configuration management database, governance policies and workflow approvals to establish those limits.
In a demonstration, ServiceNow configured a third-party customer service agent to process refunds below $25 while disabling unrelated capabilities. An $18 refund proceeded automatically, but a $40 request was rejected at runtime because it exceeded the threshold for human review.
‘Dimmer switch’ for agents
The approach supports graduated responses when agents exceed their authority. Organizations can pause an agent by revoking session tokens, restrict its access to approved tools and endpoints or deactivate it by revoking credentials. Agents can subsequently be restored with a recorded explanation.
“It’s more like a dimmer switch,” Bardoliwalla said. “You monitor, you pause, you restrict, and eventually, if necessary, you deactivate.”
Nvidia Corp. is a design and launch partner, linking AI Passport with its Open Agent Safety Platform, including the OpenShell secure runtime and Sentry security framework. The integration connects enterprise policies with enforcement within the infrastructure where agents operate.
The central implementation challenge is “making your enterprise policy meaningful at the point of execution,” said Itay Ozery, Nvidia’s director of product marketing for cybersecurity.
ServiceNow said AI Passport uses open specifications so other governance products, identity providers and enforcement systems can issue and verify credentials. It is intended to support third-party agents as well as ServiceNow’s own.
AI Control Tower is also expanding discovery, observability and financial oversight. Additions include shadow AI detection, more than 400 vendor connectors for discovery, access mapping and monitoring of agent behavior. Cost capabilities track spending by user, department and runtime, while connecting consumption and quality with business value.
AI Cost Management consolidates spending on frontier models, AI embedded in software services, hyperscalers and data center graphics processing units. A separate Operational Resilience offering brings governance, risk and security together for financial institutions.
Employee controls
The EmployeeWorks updates extend that governance strategy into everyday work. Its third-generation employee-focused AI harness combines reasoning, memory and connections to business systems, with administrator-defined controls over what employees can build and access.
Productivity Assistants target work requiring context specific to a job or business function. Employees can customize behavior, information sources and tools. Initial offerings include research and calendaring assistants, along with human resources-focused assistants for talent insights, HR business partners and managers.
Productivity Routines handle repeatable work in the background. A sales employee, for example, could automate reviewing upcoming meetings, researching prospects and assembling account materials before the workday begins.
“There’s no coding required. It’s drag and configure and deploy all within these guardrails,” said Bhavin Shah, senior vice president of ServiceNow’s employee experience group.
For developers, the new ToolSmith environment builds tools and integrations from natural-language instructions. ServiceNow said ToolSmith is trained on more than 75,000 application programming interfaces and can plan integrations, retrieve logs, suggest fixes and support testing. Shah said it uses governed connectors to read and write enterprise data in a preproduction development environment.
A Conversations API lets organizations embed EmployeeWorks capabilities in internal applications, kiosks, messaging services and other AI applications.
NTT Data Inc. is using AI Control Tower to address shadow IT and is beginning to adopt EmployeeWorks, said Jamie Robins, head of the company’s ServiceNow practice. Among the challenges the company faces are overlapping AI tools, duplicate use cases and fragmented employee systems. NTT Data hopes to simplify employees’ access to services while consolidation continues. “It takes time to consolidate processes, systems, tools, data,” he said during a product briefing.
Pricing combines seat-based licenses with bundled AI credits called assists. Customers needing additional capacity can purchase more credits, and EmployeeWorks uses the same currency as ServiceNow’s other AI products. Bardoliwalla said the model aims to balance predictable budgets with flexibility for customers whose usage grows beyond their initial entitlement.
AI Passport, shadow AI detection and AI Cost Management will be available later this quarter. Operational Resilience for financial services is available now. The new EmployeeWorks assistants, routines, harness, ToolSmith and Conversations API are in controlled availability.

articles.title: 1 milliard de messages frauduleux plus tard, Microsoft frappe un gigantesque réseau de phishing
articles.text:
Microsoft a mené une vaste opération contre un réseau qui fournissait comptes, infrastructures et faux sites web aux escrocs du monde entier. Des domaines ont été saisis et plus de 20 000 comptes désactivés pour perturber les activités de plusieurs kits de phishing et d’une place de marché clandestine.
Plus d’un milliard de mails et de SMS malveillants envoyés depuis janvier 2026 : en moins de dix mois, trois kits de phishing auraient contribué à des campagnes ciblant plus de 75 000 organisations dans plus de 150 pays, selon Microsoft. L’enquête a débuté fin 2025, après des signalements d’escroqueries au Japon. En remontant la piste de ces messages, les chercheurs ont découvert un marché clandestin fournissant aux cybercriminels des kits proposant des milliers de modèles de pages frauduleuses, mais aussi des comptes Microsoft et Google pour mener leurs attaques.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Des milliers de faux sites prêts à l’emploi pour piéger les internautes
Dans le détail, Microsoft a identifié trois kits de phishing, baptisés CoGUI, Haozi et Iron Man System, développés au sein d’un écosystème cybercriminel sinophone. Utilisé depuis au moins octobre 2024, CoGUI servait à usurper l’identité de grandes marques comme Amazon, PayPay, Apple ou Rakuten, principalement au Japon. Les messages frauduleux redirigeaient leurs destinataires vers de fausses pages de connexion ou de paiement, conçues pour récupérer leurs identifiants et leurs coordonnées bancaires.
À partir de juin 2026, Iron Man System a progressivement gagné du terrain. Les chercheurs de Resecurity, qui en ont acheté une licence pour l’étudier, ont recensé 2 360 modèles de pages frauduleuses imitant des banques, des services postaux, des administrations fiscales ou encore des opérateurs télécoms dans 130 pays et territoires.
Iron Man System transmettait aussi en temps réel les informations saisies par les victimes sur ces fausses pages. Les escrocs pouvaient recevoir des alertes sur Telegram, suivre les actions de leurs cibles et choisir ce qui s’afficherait ensuite à l’écran. Pour échapper aux systèmes de détection, le kit disposait de faux CAPTCHA, de restrictions géographiques et de listes d’adresses IP autorisées ou bloquées.
Ces trois kits étaient commercialisés via YAM Store, une place de marché clandestine qui approvisionnait aussi leurs opérateurs en comptes Microsoft et Google piratés ou obtenus en usurpant l’identité d’organisations dont les noms de domaine avaient expiré, ainsi qu’en espaces de stockage cloud détournés.
Une opération coordonnée pour neutraliser une partie des infrastructures du réseau
Pour remonter jusqu’aux opérateurs de ce réseau, Microsoft a travaillé avec la police nationale japonaise, le Japan Cybercrime Control Center (JC3) et plusieurs entreprises de cybersécurité, parmi lesquelles Resecurity, Cloudflare et Proofpoint. Les campagnes ayant également visé des organisations de santé, Health-ISAC, une association spécialisée dans le partage de renseignements sur les cybermenaces dans ce secteur, s’est jointe à Microsoft pour engager une action judiciaire.
Grâce à une décision du tribunal fédéral du district sud de la Floride, les deux organisations ont pu saisir et rediriger des noms de domaine utilisés par YAM Store, CoGUI et Iron Man System, trois composantes d’un réseau criminel plus vaste. Microsoft a également désactivé plus de 20 000 comptes associés à la place de marché et déjà bloqué plus de 100 000 domaines utilisés pour des opérations d’usurpation d’identité et de fraude.
À noter enfin que sur le milliard de messages frauduleux attribués à cet écosystème, plus de 750 millions ciblaient des clients de Microsoft. Selon l’entreprise, ces campagnes auraient rapporté plusieurs dizaines de millions de dollars à leurs opérateurs.

articles.title: When it came to Cal AI's viral success, a small army of influencers paid off | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Zach Yadegari has enjoyed an immense amount of success for someone who only recently graduated from high school. Founder of the AI-fueled calorie tracking app Cal AI, Yadegari is only 19 but his company has rocketed to viral fame over the past two years. At TechCrunch Disrupt on Thursday, Yadegari shared details of that surprising rise to prominence.
Cal AI, which was founded in 2024, exploded onto the internet thanks largely to Yadegari’s strategy of deploying a small army of influencers to promote the brand. The company generated over $30 million in revenue in two years and was acquired by MyFitnessPal for an undisclosed amount of money in March.
Discussing his social strategy onstage, Yadegari noted that an early sign of success came when an influencer’s post about them led to approximately a thousand new users over the course of two days.
“From there, we figured out, okay, this can actually work for us, and so we started recruiting influencers as fast as we could — paying as many people as possible to start posting for us,” he said. “What we saw was that it was a clear formula. It was pretty linear, but it was extremely fast. I guess linear in the sense that every post they did would get a certain number of viewers that would convert.”
The Forbes 30 Under 30 alumnus told the audience that part of his company’s strategy was to negotiate rates with influencers, promising them certain payouts for a certain scale of reach. A lot of influencers are “broke college kids” who “just want cash,” Yadegari added. “You just ask them, okay, we’ll pay you this, but we need to get us at least this amount of use and keep posting until you get there.”
Another important component of success was finding the right influencers whose reach can be quantified. “The biggest thing for us was finding influencers that had very tight communities,” the founder said.
Yadegari, whose father was in the audience, also credited his family with giving him the freedom to go after his ambitions. Does he also credit higher education for his success? Not so much.
“I think the only real reason to go to college is if you want to have a fun social time as a kid and be with other people,” he said, to audience laughter.
Earlier this month, Yadegari also launched Persona, a new AI agent startup that has already raised $10 million.
Yadegari said the “overarching mission” with Persona is to “make computing seamless with human life.” The company’s personal AI assistant will “live anyplace with internet connection,” he said, including “iMessage, app, email, phone call.” He added that part of what distinguishes the company’s plans for this AI assistant is to build a “hardware ecosystem around” the app.

articles.title: HUSB237: The Cost-Effective PD Sink with Just 2 Passives - EE Times
articles.text:
Driven by the EU Common Charger Directive (Regulation (EU) 2022/2380), consumer and industrial electronics manufacturers worldwide are accelerating the migration from traditional DC barrel jack power input to unified USB Type-C PD interfaces.
For the various of power devices, such as IoT devices, wireless chargers, power tools, smart speakers, drones and portable rechargeable devices, is there a simple way to upgrade the device with barrel DC port to a Type-C PD solutions.
Right now, Hynetek Semiconductor launches HUSB237, a fully standalone hardware-configured USB PD sink controller specially optimized for Type-C to DC barrel jack conversion scenarios. The HUSB237 delivers a rapid, software-free upgrade from DC barrel connectors to Type-C, thanks to its ultra-simplified peripheral design and the compact DFN2x2-6L package.
The HUSB237 is a highly integrated standalone USB PD sink controller supporting maximum 100W (20V/5A) power rating, integrating complete CC logic, USB PD protocol and legacy protocols on a single chip. It eliminates reliance on external MCU or firmware programming, and only requires two external components for normal operation, drastically reducing system BOM count and PCB layout difficulty.
Regarding the left two external components, one is the de-coupled ceramic cap placed at the VBUS pin, just for filtering the input power noise. The reset one is a resistor or a capacitor at VSET pin. The target requested voltage is set purely by this part. Just choosing different values (as shown in the next picture), the HUSB237 can cover mainstream fixed voltages for DC barrel equipment.
- Target Application Scenarios
The HUSB237 is tailor-made for all equipment migrating from legacy DC barrel jack to USB-C PD power input, covering high-volume cost-sensitive markets:
- USB-C to DC barrel jack conversion cables & adapter dongles
- Low-to-medium power wireless charging pads
- Consumer IoT devices: smart speakers, portable humidifiers, cameras
- Small power tools, mini drones, handheld rechargeable gadgets
- Any fixed-voltage rechargeable equipment requiring universal Type-C PD power supply
Besides the HUSB237, Hynetek provides a complete PD sink product family to cover diversified design requirements from low-power to high-power, hardware fixed to software programmable scenarios:
Position: Standard certified PD sink controller within 100W power rating
Core strengths: USB-IF (TID:3666) , I²C programmable multi-voltage PDO, DFN 3×3-10L package
Best fit: Products requiring official USB certification, multi-voltage adjustable end devices
Position: High-power PD3.1 EPR sink controller up to 240W (48V/5A)
Core strengths: Support AVS fine voltage adjustment, withstand high-voltage industrial power supply
Best fit: High-power peripherals, server accessories, industrial portable equipment demanding 240W PD
Position: 240W USB PD Sink and 5V PD Source Controller
Core strengths: Standalone Controller with I2C Interface
Best fit: Mid-tier smart consumer devices with limited software debugging budget
Position: 140W Type-C DRP controller with MCU
Core strengths: Support 28V 5A maximum power rating at USB Type-C connector pins
Best fit: Travel adapters, car chargers,energy store system
Position: 100W USB PD DRP controller with MCU
Core strengths: Support 20V 5A maximum power rating
Best fit: Battery‑powered equipment, monitors, small‑size power tools
Position: 240W USB PD DRP controller for 48V EPR applications
Core strengths: Support 48V 5A maximum power rating with more than 60V tolerance
Best fit: Electric power tools,gaming Notebooks,storage systems
Conclusion
With the global move toward unified USB-C interface, the HUSB237 addresses the key challenges manufacturers face when upgrading products with DC barrel jacks: high cost, complex circuit layout, and software development effort.
As the most cost-effective standalone PD sink controller in Hynetek’s portfolio, it provides a plug-and-play, hardware-only Type-C PD solution for mass-market fixed-voltage devices. For more product specifications,
visit the official website: www.hynetek.com

articles.title: Jordi Wild culmina su transformación en "el Joe Rogan español" y entrevistará a Feijóo y Abascal en plena campaña
articles.text:
En las generales de 2023, Jordi Wild ya quiso llevar a los grandes candidatos a The Wild Project y la idea se quedó en nada. Para el próximo 29N le ha bastado un vídeo lanzando la idea de entrevistar a los tres principales candidatos. Feijóo y Abascal aceptaron en horas, y el entorno de Sánchez le había escrito antes incluso de que lanzara la invitación.
Las últimas noticias. Jordi Wild ha publicado en X una actualización de su "Semana especial elecciones" con el estado de las negociaciones. Alberto Núñez Feijóo aceptó a las horas del llamamiento y Santiago Abascal, poco después. Con Pedro Sánchez la conversación empezó antes: según el relato de Wild, alguien "muy cercano" al presidente le escribió la víspera del anuncio para hablar de una charla en el podcast, y la respuesta está ahora en manos del equipo del presidente, así que muy posiblemente pronto se anunciará su presencia en el programa.
Otra historia. En 2023 la cosa fue distinta. Wild también trató de sentar a los cabezas de lista de las elecciones y la iniciativa no llegó a materializarse. Sánchez prefirió entonces el pódcast La Pija y la Quinqui, que le brindó una relevancia e imagen de cercanía muy importante. Tres años después, los partidos se acercan a Jordi para negociar bajo sus condiciones.
Las condiciones. Wild quiere al número uno de cada lista y no a un portavoz, y no entrega las preguntas por adelantado. Para la grabación plantea charlas de 50 a 90 minutos, y con un pacto: él no edita nada y los candidatos no pueden pedir que se corte ninguna parte. Y si uno de los tres no quiere acudir a la propuesta, no entrevista a ninguno. Su idea es publicar las entrevistas a partir del 9 de noviembre, aún en precampaña. Feijóo contestó en un vídeo en TikTok que se sentaba "cuando quieras" y bromeó con que aquello era "más fácil que meterse en un ring contigo", en alusión a las veladas de lucha que organiza Wild. Abascal se limitó a un "cuenta conmigo". Los candidatos tienen diez días para responder antes de que Jordi plantee un ultimátum.
Falta el cuarto. La regla del todo o nada da a cada invitado, en la práctica, un veto sobre los demás, y además hay una cuarta silla que aún no tiene dueño. Wild espera noticias de "Sumar, Frente Amplio, Podemos, y la coalición de izquierdas". IU, Más Madrid, Movimiento Sumar y los comuns propusieron el 12 de octubre a Ada Colau como candidata del Frente Amplio, mientras Podemos va por libre y ha pactado con ERC para Cataluña. El registro de coaliciones se cierra este viernes 16, así que posiblemente de cara a la semana que viene sepamos si la coalición de izquierdas acepta la invitación de Jordi.
El Rogan de Manresa. The Wild Project fue el pódcast más escuchado de Spotify en España en 2024, y aunque cayó al cuarto puesto en el ranking de 2025, recibió ese mismo año el premio a la trayectoria de los Ondas Globales del Podcast, y su productora facturó 2,4 millones de euros en 2024. En el mismo resumen de 2025, Spotify situaba por encima del 40% el crecimiento del videopódcast en España, el formato en el que Wild nació y que ha cambiado cómo se consume el pódcast.
¿Es de derechas? La imagen pública de Wild se encuadra hacia la derecha, como analiza ESDiario, y quizás eso podría complicar la presencia de Sánchez (que por otra parte no ha tenido nunca miedo de enfrentarse a némesis como Ana Rosa Quintana). Wild, además, arrastra acusaciones de machismo desde su etapa de youtuber y de blanquear a la extrema derecha. En su torneo de lucha, el Dogfight Wild Tournament se coreó "Pedro Sánchez, hijo de puta", cánticos que el propio Wild lamentó porque le perjudican. En septiembre, la ficha de su episodio con el periodista Ignacio Cembrero prometía explicar la "desconcertante y servil actitud" de Sánchez ante Mohamed VI.
El precedente de Rogan. El locutor al que Jordi Wild admira sentó a Donald Trump el 25 de octubre de 2024 durante casi tres horas en su estudio de Texas. El episodio superó los 35 millones de visualizaciones en YouTube el lunes siguiente, y el verificador de CNN contó al menos 32 afirmaciones falsas en la conversación. Un año después de perder las elecciones, Kamala Harris admitió que lamentaba no haber ido al programa de Rogan. Ese debate estadounidense sobre si la izquierda debe pisar esos estudios llega a España con un matiz: Sánchez no ha tenido reparos en acudir a formatos alejados de la entrevista política clásica. Pero aún se espera la confirmación.

articles.title: Jio's Akash Ambani says services, not tariff hikes, to drive revenue as record IPO nears
articles.text:
Jio's Akash Ambani says services, not tariff hikes, to drive revenue as record IPO nears
Ambani said Jio charges about Rs 4.9 per gigabyte against an industry average of Rs 7.5, with customers using 43.7 GB a month.
Jio Platforms plans to raise revenue per customer mainly by selling more services rather than lifting tariffs, though it keeps the option of higher prices, Managing Director Akash Ambani said on Thursday, days before the Reliance Industries unit opens what would be India's largest initial public offering.
"We always have the ability to take up prices," Ambani told a press conference in Mumbai, but the company would rather give customers more services and charge for them than rely on price per gigabyte as its main lever.
Asked whether a tariff increase was coming, he gave no timeline. He said telecom spending per user as a share of India's per-capita income had roughly halved to about 1% since Jio's 2016 launch, which he called headroom.
Chief Executive Pankaj Pawar said tariffs were only one of several levers.
Ambani said Jio charges about Rs 4.9 per gigabyte against an industry average of Rs 7.5, with customers using 43.7 GB a month.
"We expect a USD 1.4-trillion digital economy by FY31; we will take a huge market share of this," Ambani said, naming mobile, home broadband and enterprise and international services as the growth engines.
He said Jio carries more than 60% of India's wireless data traffic.
New services outside Jio's licensed telecom business, such as a voice-AI feature announced at Reliance's annual meeting, could push its EBITDA margin above the current level. The margin was 53.3 per cent in April-June, up from about 50% three years ago, he added.
On overseas expansion, Ambani said Jio would offer its in-house network technology to foreign operators as a managed-service partner, not by selling hardware or software licences, and without heavy capital spending.
He said the split between domestic and international revenue would become clear "as we sign on our first customers".
India accounted for 96.62% of revenue in the year to March 2026, according to the company's prospectus, which gives no figures for overseas sales.
Jio set a price band of Rs 1,065 to 1,119 a share for its offer of up to 27 crore new shares, about 3% of existing capital, with no offer-for-sale component.
At the top of the band, the sale would raise about Rs 30,213 crore, ahead of Hyundai Motor India's Rs 27,870 crore share sale in October 2024, the country's biggest.
The price implies a market value of about Rs 10.3 lakh crore, short of the roughly Rs 11 lakh crore the company had earlier been said to seek.
Bidding runs from October 21 to 23, with anchor investors bidding on October 19. Shares are expected to begin trading on October 28. Proceeds will go toward prepaying borrowings of Reliance Jio Infocomm, the telecom subsidiary, and general corporate purposes, according to the October 14 red herring prospectus.
Reliance Jio Infocomm served 533.3 million customers at June-end, including 284.9 million on 5G, which Ambani said was the largest 5G base outside China. Average revenue per user rose to Rs 215.6 a month.
Average monthly data consumption per customer reached 43.7 GB in the first quarter of FY27.
The company reported EBITDA of Rs 76,225 crore in FY26, with a compound annual growth rate of 17.8% between FY24 and FY26. Its EBITDA margin stood at 53.3% in the first quarter of FY27, he said.
Ambani called home broadband the biggest growth engine, citing industry-wide additions of about 340 million 4G and 5G customers between fiscal 2026 and 2031 as another driver. Jio had 28.6 million fixed broadband customers and took 67.5% of India's net fixed additions in fiscal 2026, he said.
Reliance Industries owns 66.43% of Jio Platforms.
Meta Platforms affiliate Jaadhu Holdings holds 9.98% and Google International 7.73%. Nineteen banks, including Kotak Mahindra Capital, Morgan Stanley, BofA Securities, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Citi, are managing the offer.
Ambani outlined a strategy built around technology, digital connectivity and infrastructure, supported by three growth engines: mobility, home broadband, and enterprise and international services.
Jio's technology platform, which Ambani described as an end-to-end technology stack, is central to the strategy. Its connectivity business provides access to 533.3 million customers, and its infrastructure includes 3,60,537 towers and 26,800 MHz of spectrum.
In mobility, Jio expects industry-wide additions of 340 million 4G and 5G customers between FY26 and FY31, creating opportunities for higher average revenue per user (ARPU), a key measure of telecom operators' revenue-generating capacity.
Home broadband is another growth driver. Jio had 28.6 million fixed broadband customers and accounted for 67.5 per cent of India's net fixed broadband additions in FY26.
In enterprise services, Jio is targeting India's estimated Rs 5.1 trillion addressable market for digital services in FY26. It also plans to monetise its technology stack in selected overseas markets.
Ambani highlighted the transformation in India's digital connectivity since Jio entered the telecom market in 2016, when average download speeds were about 2.5 Mbps. They have since risen to around 68 Mbps nationally.
He said Jio's average 5G download speed was 198.9 Mbps, roughly twice that of competing operators over the preceding three years. The company also highlighted the sharp decline in data costs since its entry into the market, saying its current pricing stood among the lowest globally.
The expansion of affordable mobile data has helped drive higher consumption of online video, digital payments and other internet services, while the rollout of 5G and fixed broadband is opening additional opportunities for telecom operators to monetise data demand.
Ambani said the company's goal was to help make India a leading digital society, with Jio serving as a partner in that transformation.
He pitched Jio Platforms as a technology company rather than a mobile carrier, saying it will sell its in-house network software and equipment to overseas operators, though the business remains overwhelmingly domestic.

articles.title: Apple dévoilerait de nouveaux produits très attendus avant la fin du mois, voici ce qu’il faut savoir
articles.text:
Autant dire que le calendrier d’Apple est actuellement chargé. L’entreprise à la pomme vient de dévoiler le HomeView, la nouvelle Apple TV 4K, le HomePod mini 2, ainsi que 9 objets pour la maison en partenariat avec LG. Par ailleurs, ce 23 octobre, l’iPhone Duo, soit le premier téléphone pliant de l’entreprise, sera officiellement commercialisé. Et cela n’est pas tout, puisque Apple a prévu un nouvel événement en ce mois d’octobre 2026 pour dévoiler encore de nouveaux produits.
De nouveaux produits Apple devraient être dévoilés le 27 octobre 2026
Comme le rapporte le toujours très bien informé Mark Gurman, journaliste chez Bloomberg, Apple a prévu un événement d’une journée entière à Los Angeles le mardi 27 octobre 2026. Aucune retransmission en direct de l’événement n’est prévue. Des communiqués de presse seront envoyés aux journalistes et certains d’entre eux seront conviés à prendre en main les nouveaux appareils de la marque.
Mais de quels appareils est-il question ? Mark Gurman laisse peu de doute à ce sujet. Apple devrait dévoiler un MacBook Pro équipé d’un écran OLED tactile (proposé en 14 ou 16 pouces), un nouvel iPad mini doté d’un écran OLED, un MacBook Pro M6 d’entrée de gamme et un iMac M6. Bien entendu, ces informations devront être confirmées le 27 octobre prochain.
Il faut s’attendre à des prix particulièrement élevés
Mark Gurman s’attend à des prix élevés pour ces nouveaux produits : « je pense qu’ils seront assez chers, ce qui ne devrait pas vraiment surprendre compte tenu du contexte actuel ». Il faut dire que la crise de la mémoire ne faiblit pas, bien au contraire.
Il reste également à connaître la date de commercialisation de ces nouveaux produits. Ils pourraient être mis sur le marché le jour de leur présentation, ou certains d’entre eux pourraient connaître un lancement décalé, à l’image de l’iPhone Duo. Dans tous les cas, ces produits devraient être commercialisés avant Noël.
En l’espace d’un mois, nous aurons donc eu droit à trois événements Apple : la keynote de rentrée, l’événement « Welcome Home » dédié aux appareils domotiques de l’entreprise et une conférence centrée sur les Mac. Nous vous en parlions récemment, Apple aurait décidé de changer de stratégie, notamment en lançant de nouveaux produits tout au long de l’année, et ce mois d’octobre semble confirmer cette orientation.

articles.title: Alienware AW3226Q 32-inch 4K OLED gaming monitor review: Sleek design with performance and value to match
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
Aside from a lack of practical gamma adjustments, the Alienware AW3226Q delivers a bright, colorful, and razor-sharp image. With solid game performance and even more solid value, it’s an attractive choice.
Reasons to buy
- + Extremely sharp and detailed image
- + Accurate color before and after calibration
- + Bright and contrasty HDR
- + Dolby Vision support
- + Premium build quality
- + Good value
Reasons to avoid
- - Light gamma out of the box
- - Missing calibration options requires some compromise
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
Though OLEDs remain a premium gaming monitor category, there is no denying that they make up a large share of new model introductions. Looking over my reviews for the past two years, they represent just over half of the screens that have crossed my test bench. Prices are trickling down, and one company trying to make the best OLED gaming monitors more affordable is Alienware. Though it has plenty of high-end displays available, the newest models are aimed at more modest budgets.
The latest example is one that would have been a flagship not too long ago. The AW3226Q is a 32-inch 4K flat OLED with Tandem Stripe RGB technology, 165 Hz, Adaptive-Sync, HDR400 True Black, Dolby Vision, and wide gamut color. Let’s take a look.
Alienware AW3226Q Specs
| Panel Type / Backlight | Tandem RGB Stripe Organic Light Emitting Diode | 
| Screen Size / Aspect Ratio | 32 inches / 16:9 | 
| Max Resolution and Refresh Rate | 3840x2160 @ 165 Hz | 
| Row 3 - Cell 0 | FreeSync and G-Sync Compatible | 
| Native Color Depth and Gamut | 10-bit / DCI-P3 | 
| Row 5 - Cell 0 | HDR400 True Black, HDR10, Dolby Vision | 
| Response Time (GTG) | 0.03ms | 
| Brightness (mfr) | 250 nits full field | 
| Row 8 - Cell 0 | 1,000 nits HDR 3% window | 
| Contrast | Unmeasurable | 
| Speakers | None | 
| Video Inputs | 1x DisplayPort 1.4 | 
| Row 12 - Cell 0 | 2x HDMI 2.1 | 
| Audio | 3.5mm headphone output | 
| USB 3.0 | 1x up, 2x down, 1x USB-C (15w) | 
| Power Consumption | 34w, brightness @ 200 nits | 
| Panel Dimensions WxHxD w/base | 28.2 x 19.2-23.5 x 9.1 inches (716 x 488-597 x 232mm) | 
| Panel Thickness | 2.3 inches (57mm) | 
| Bezel Width | Top/sides: 0.31 inch (8mm) | 
| Row 19 - Cell 0 | Bottom: 0.55 inch (14mm) | 
| Weight | 17.05 pounds (7.75kg) | 
| Warranty | 3 years | 
Tandem RGB Stripe is the newest OLED variant, and it can be found in the AW3226Q as well as several new screens from Asus. I propose to simply call it TRS-OLED in this review. It takes the approach of stacking emissive layers to provide more light with less power consumption. It also broadens the color gamut to over 100% coverage of DCI-P3. In Alienware’s case, it’s four emissive layers behind an RGB sub-pixel layer that acts as a polarizer. By putting the pixels next to each other, hence the Stripe, rather than the triangular arrangement of QD-OLEDs, you get a wide color gamut and high brightness with sharper detail and no chance of fringing.
The AW3226Q produces 1,000 nits from a 3% window in HDR mode and around 275 nits full field as I measured it. The polarizing layer makes blacks more true by keeping ambient reflections from spoiling the image. Color volume came in at 101% of DCI-P3, which is more than a typical OLED, although a bit less than one equipped with Quantum Dots. And power consumption is low, with just 34 watts drawn at 200 nits brightness. HDR10 and Dolby Vision are supported, with a VESA DisplayHDR 400 True Black certification that I verified in testing.
Gamers benefit from the AW3226Q’s 165 Hz refresh rate that works with Adaptive-Sync to produce smooth motion processing. Like all speedy OLEDs, input lag is low and, in my tests, it managed to beat one 240 Hz screen that costs a good deal more. You also get AlienVision, which is a super cool aiming point and sniper mode editor that is unique to Alienware displays.
The AW3226Q is attractively styled and well-appointed with USB ports, a bit of LED lighting, and a solid stand with full ergonomics. It includes a DisplayPort 1.4 input and two HDMI 2.1 ports with FRL (48Gbps) and eARC, making it easy to integrate the monitor with soundbars or AV systems that also support HDMI eARC. There are no internal speakers, but you do get a 3.5mm headphone jack. Also included are USB ports: two Type-A, one Type-B, and one Type-C.
The AW3226Q is a decent value at its opening price of $699. That’s a significant discount over the $1,000 you’ll spend on an AW3225QF, which only has minor differences.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Assembly and Accessories
The AW3226Q arrived in fully recyclable packaging consisting of a clamshell-style carton and molded pulp forms to protect the contents. The upright snaps onto the panel and the base attaches with a captive bolt. The resulting piece is solid and stable on the desktop. The power supply is internal, so you get a stout IEC cord plus cables for DisplayPort, HDMI, and USB-A/B.
Product 360
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
The AW3226Q’s screen is touted as “almost frameless”, and indeed, it is. The top and side frames are just 8mm, while at the bottom, it’s 14mm and flush on all sides. There is no extra protruding trim. The bottom is not without utility, though, as it puts a headphone jack and two USB ports within easy reach. The remaining I/O is in the usual spot, up and under, where you’ll find a DisplayPort 1.4, two HDMI 2.1, and more USBs, one upstream and one downstream.
The stand features Alienware’s latest design where the upright’s attachment point appears to float above the base. There are no sharp edges or square corners here. Everything is smoothly tapered, including the bulge in the back, which is generously vented around its perimeter. On one side is the Alienware head, which has the main LED feature. It can light up in a variety of colors and effects, all controlled from the OSD.
The upright has an angled cable management hole, which is cool because then you can’t see through it from the front. It features 5/21 degrees tilt, 20 degrees swivel, a 90-degree portrait mode, and 4.3 inches of height range. Movements are smooth and firm with no wobble or play. If you’d rather use an aftermarket support, the stand comes off to expose a 100mm VESA mount with fasteners included.
OSD Features
Pressing the AW3226Q’s joystick opens a well-stocked OSD with nearly every option a gamer or enthusiast could want. Except for one that I’ll tell you about below.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
The first joystick press opens a quick menu with info at the top that shows resolution, refresh, current preset, HDR mode, panel health, and the dark stabilizer setting. At the bottom of the screen is a quick menu that can be programmed by the user. Fun fact: that thatch-roof house in the photo is down the street from where Jane Austen lived from 1809 to 1817 in Chawton, England.
With another upclick, we get the full OSD, which has 11 sections starting with Game and the 12 picture modes. Standard is the default and its color is accurate, but you can get some improvement by using Custom Color and its two-point white balance sliders. Creator mode gives you access to the sRGB and DCI-P3 gamuts. The one thing missing, and this is true of every Dell and Alienware monitor I’ve ever reviewed, is a gamma control. Normally, this isn’t an issue, but in the AW3226Q’s case, the default gamma is too light with no practical way to correct. I’ll show you what I mean on page four.
Game Enhance includes a set of timers and a frame rate counter. The aiming point editor is called AlienVision, and it gets its own screen with parameters for reticle shape, color, and position. You can also roll your own sniper mode with variable magnification and opacity. There are three memories to save your configurations. Esports modes include 25 and 27-inch images with reduced resolution, which is a benefit to frame rates, although you’re still capped at 165 Hz.
AlienFX lighting refers to the Alienware head in the back and the power button LED, which you can see from the front. They can display in any color or effect or be turned off if you want total darkness.
In the Display menu, you’ll find seven HDR modes plus a toggle for Dolby Vision. I found during testing that the HDR Peak 1000 Bright mode delivered the brightest and most impactful HDR.
The AW3226Q includes full PIP/PBP functions for viewing two video sources at once. You can move the PIP window to any corner or decide how to split the PBP mode.
In Personalize, you can program the quick menu seen in the first photo above and the four joystick directions. Many functions can be accessed this way, like presets, Alienvision, headphone volume, and more.
Most of the AW3226Q’s panel maintenance is handled by an algorithm that tracks the panel’s usage and manipulates pixel brightness accordingly. You can also initiate a panel refresh routine manually if you prefer.
Alienware AW3226Q Calibration Settings
Calibrating the AW3226Q was something of a compromise. In Standard mode, color and grayscale are without visible errors, but gamma is too light. And there is no gamma control in the custom color mode. You can adjust gamma in Creator mode and select sRGB if you like, but then you give up grayscale calibration. There’s also a gamma control in Console mode, but this only works over HDMI. I have long wished that Alienware and Dell would add gamma to the options in Custom Color mode. And when they do, I hope it’s a fine resolution slider like the Asus XG27AQNGV has, not the usual presets that are 0.2 apart. Anyway, my suggested settings are below.
For HDR10 signals, you get seven specific picture modes. Desktop is the default, but for the highest brightness and impact, choose Peak 1000 Bright.
| Picture Mode | Custom Color | 
| Brightness 200 nits | 84 | 
| Brightness 120 nits | 47 | 
| Brightness 100 nits | 38 | 
| Brightness 80 nits | 28 | 
| Brightness 50 nits | 13 (min. 24 nits) | 
| Contrast | 75 | 
| Color Temp User | Gain – Red 99, Green 98, Blue 97 | 
| Row 8 - Cell 0 | Bias – Red 50, Green 50, Blue 50 | 
Gaming and Hands-on
Gameplay on the AW3226Q was satisfying and successful. But it didn’t quite have the shooting-fish-in-a-barrel feel of some of the 240 Hz monitors I’ve experienced. Motion was smooth and quick, but I had to concentrate a bit more on my aim to make sure I wasn’t wasting ammo. I’m in nit-pick mode here because I play on so many different monitors. After a short time, I adapted to the AW3226Q and was handily dispatching gory monsters and aliens in Doom Eternal.
Frame rates stayed at 165fps thanks to a GeForce RTX 4090, and there was only a slight amount of motion blur. The picture didn’t smear like some slower screens, but there was just a little less definition in hard edges when I moved the mouse quickly. Again, it was something I noticed, then adapted to. I played with the AlienVision options a bit and found them very useful. And once I had created a couple of setups, I could switch them on and off quickly using the programmable menu and joystick options.
The AW3226Q was a monitor I could easily live with long term. The image is gorgeous for starters. Tandem RGB Stripe OLEDs (TRS-OLEDs) are sharper than other variants, by enough that you can tell the difference in a side-by-side comparison. I spend a lot of time in Photoshop, and this monitor is easily on par with the best professional displays I’ve reviewed. It’s also colorful and accurate. I noted light gamma during testing, which only had a minor effect. It wasn’t that I found the picture lacking; it was that I didn’t have a practical option to darken the gamma to my liking.
In a nutshell, Standard mode has no adjustments. Custom Color lets you tweak grayscale with a two-point control, but there are no gamma presets. Creator has color gamut options for sRGB and DCI-P3 and gamma presets, but no RGB sliders. So, whatever you choose, there’s a compromise.
Physically, the AW3226Q is a presence in a good way. I love Alienware’s newest styling aesthetic, which has been around for a while now. The almost frameless screen delivers on its promise. When the picture is on, the bezel disappears. Taking away the bottom trim strip makes a big difference there. Though I missed internal speakers, I appreciated the inclusion of USB ports, especially the ones right under the bezel. They, along with the headphone jack, are within easy reach. And even though it is a value-oriented display, it has the same premium build quality and solid feel as Alienware’s flagship models.
Takeaway: The AW3226Q has a gorgeous image with super crisp detail and deep texture. Its Tandem RGB Stripe technology eliminates any hint of fringing and gives the picture more dimension. The 165 Hz refresh rate produced a little blur, but I soon adapted to it. I reminded myself that the lower number comes with a $200 cost savings. My favorite use for the AW3226Q was as an everyday screen. It’s a premium tool for Photoshop or any graphics app you might wish to use. And it makes a great personal TV as well thanks to its support for Dolby Vision and HDMI eARC. Just hook up an external AV system or soundbar, and you’ve got a desktop home theater.
